When Integrity determines that a SIN is compromised, the investigator adds a fraud warning in FTS using the FTS - Integrity Fraud Indicator transaction. The Integrity investigator advises the client that a detailed security check may be required in the future to validate the client’s identity. When the warning is activated, the SIN field on the tombstone data is highlighted in red and a red warning symbol shows next to the field. The fraud warning remains on the file until Integrity removes it. Only Integrity investigators can add or remove the warning. The fraud warning only shows in FTS and has no impact on the other systems. It serves as an alert that the client has been a fraud victim. The IPOC officer follows the current RPAN procedures, but takes extra precautions when a fraud warning is present. Officers must not inform clients that the fraud warning is on the file. The IPOC officer follows the fact-finding procedures and refers to Communication: Client identity validation for telephone discussions — Instructions for information on validating the client’s identity. When actioning an IPOC SN Returned payment WI, the IPOC officer may also notice suspicious activities on a client’s file, such as multiple applications in NWS or multiple changes to the client’s banking information. Before actioning the IPOC SN Returned payment WI, the IPOC officer determines if: the file has been referred to Integrity due to potentially fraudulent activities; fraud indicators are present; a 71 - Integrity Services case manual action (MA71) must be input; the returned payment is potentially fraudulent. The IPOC officer refers to Fraud indicators: Identifying potentially fraudulent claims — Knowledge for a detailed list of known fraud indicators. Fraud indicators: Identifying potentially fraudulent claims — Knowledge In addition to these fraud indicators, the returned payment reason is often, but not exclusively, Account frozen . If fraud is suspected, the IPOC officer terminates the direct deposit. The IPOC officer does not fact-find with the client, but refers the issue to Integrity and inputs an MA71. If an MA71 or a 71 - Integrity Services case disentitlement (D71) has been imposed and there is no outstanding Action Item (AI) assigned to Integrity, the IPOC officer creates an AI WI to inform Integrity that a potentially fraudulent payment has been returned. Potentially fraudulent payment A returned payment is potentially fraudulent when there is a doubt that the payment is not legitimate (i.e. the client did not request the payment or the legitimate payment was redirected to a third party who changed the client’s personal information). A returned payment is not potentially fraudulent when: The returned payment is for a claim that is not potentially fraudulent and fraud indicators are present for another BPC. This typically occurs when a previous legitimate BPC is recalculated due to new information received or when a family supplement (FS) recalculation results in an underpayment (UP) and fraud indicators are present for the active claim. The returned payment was issued before a potentially fraudulent renewal or before a third party changed the client’s personal information. If the returned payment is not potentially fraudulent, the IPOC officer replaces the payment if the address or the banking information on file are legitimate. If the IPOC officer doubts that the address or banking information on file are not legitimate because the client’s personal information has been compromised, the IPOC officer does not replace the returned payment. If the returned payment is potentially fraudulent, the IPOC officer moves the IPOC SN Returned payment WI to Pending for 15 business days from the date the original payment was returned. This gives the client the opportunity to contact Service Canada. After 15 business days, if the client has requested a payment replacement, the IPOC officer replaces the payment in SPS. If the client has not requested a payment replacement, the IPOC officer documents this information in an SROC, cancels the payment in SPS and creates an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction to cancel the returned payment. The IPOC officer also requests that a 39 - Prevent payment of Part II benefits and/or incorrect Part I benefits disentitlement (D39) be input to prevent the payment from being reissued to a potential third party until the investigation is completed. When a returned payment for a blocked claim is not potentially fraudulent, but an MA71 is present or must be input on the active claim due to potentially fraudulent third party activities, the IPOC officer does not contact the client to update the address or direct deposit information on file. The IPOC officer determines if the address or direct deposit information has been updated to replace the returned payment. If new information is not available or the address or direct deposit information on file is potentially fraudulent, the IPOC officer follows guidance for undeliverable payment. Potentially fraudulent payment on a continuing claim A client’s personal information may have been compromised and used multiple times by a third party in an attempt to establish fraudulent claims and receive benefits. If there is already an active continuing EI claim in FTS, a third party may have changed the client’s direct deposit information. When a client is on a continuing claim and the Direct Deposit History (MN16) screen indicates that the banking information on file has been changed by ACPTRAN due to a new EI application received or by MEITRAN due to changes made in MSCA, the IPOC officer reviews the claim for fraud indicators. If the IPOC officer suspects that the client’s direct deposit information has been changed fraudulently while the client is receiving benefits, the IPOC officer terminates the direct deposit and does not fact-find with the client. In this case, the IPOC officer replaces the returned payment with a cheque. The IPOC officer determines if the case has been referred to Integrity and adds the information to the current AI WI or, if necessary, creates an AI WI for Integrity to investigate. Future payments are issued by cheque until the client contacts Service Canada to update the direct deposit information. If the issue is not a fraudulent change to the client’s direct deposit information while the client is on a continuing claim, the IPOC officer terminates the direct deposit and refers the issue to Integrity. The IPOC officer does not fact-find with the client and does not replace the payment. The officer refers every new case of potential fraud to Integrity by adding the new information to an existing AI WI or by creating a new AI WI. Claim Set-Up (CS) WI When a fraudulent application is filed, ACP may not be able to register the claim. When ACP cannot register the claim, it automatically creates a CS WI for processing. The processing officer actioning the CS WI determines if fraud indicators are present and refers the issue to Integrity, if necessary. In NWS, if there is an outstanding CS WI, the IPOC officer moves the IPOC SN Returned payment WI to Pending until the processing officer completes the CS WI. If the processing officer refers the file to Integrity in an AI WI, the IPOC officer adds details to the current AI WI for Integrity to review. If there is no CS WI, but the issue has already been referred to Integrity, the IPOC officer adds details to the current AI WI for Integrity to review. Account frozen A financial institution may return a payment when they suspect that an account is being used for fraudulent activities. The returned payment reason is frequently listed as Account frozen but the financial institution may use any other reason. Financial institutions also use the returned payment reason Account frozen for reasons other than fraudulent activities. Therefore, if a financial institution uses this reason, it does not necessarily constitute proof of fraudulent activities on a claim. To suspect fraud, there must be other fraud indicators.

To ensure the client receives timely payment of all benefits payable before the vacation, any outstanding claimant’s reports for full weeks payable must be processed before imposing a manual action to stop payments (MA01) and reassigning the WI to Level 2. Claimant’s reports are for 2-week periods and are completed by the client when possible. However, the Level 1 officer may input a one-week report to ensure all payments before a vacation period are received. This requires a 2-day input. To avoid creating an overpayment (OP), weeks during which the client may not be payable due to the vacation are processed after the MA01 is imposed. An MA01 can only be imposed on an established claim; no MA01 is imposed on a skeleton (MA03) claim.

If the cancellation is not retroactive, the BP is cancelled with: an M149 - Initial Intake Data (M149) transaction if a renewal week has not been input; a File Control Data (M101) transaction type 7 (M101-7) transaction if a renewal week has been input. If the cancellation is retroactive, the officer cancels the BP with a M101-7 transaction. If weeks have been processed, the officer also does the following: If weeks have not been paid on the existing BP after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated, the officer creates an IPOC Review (IPOC REV) WI. If weeks have been paid on the existing BP after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated, the officer creates an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction. When the officer retroactively cancels a BP on which weeks have been processed after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated, an OP is created for the weeks that will be payable during the new BP. Once the OP has been established, the officer inputs an agreed deduction in PSCD equal to the benefit rate amount so that the benefits payable in the new BP are applied to the OP. For more information, the officer refers to Applying an agreed deduction in PSCD . Applying an agreed deduction in PSCD

The inputs to terminate a BP depend on whether the termination is retroactive. If the termination is not retroactive, the BP is terminated with: an M149 - Initial Intake Data (M149) transaction if the renewal week has not been input; a File Control Data (M101) transaction type 7 (M101-7) if the renewal week has been input. If the termination is retroactive, the officer terminates the BP with an M101-7 if weeks have not been processed. If weeks have been processed, the officer also creates the following: an IPOC Review (IPOC REV) WI if weeks have not been paid on the existing BP after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated; an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction if benefits have been paid on the existing BP after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated. When the officer retroactively terminates a BP on which weeks have been processed after the renewal week or after the disentitlement was terminated, an OP is created for the weeks that will be payable during the new BP. Note A medical certificate (including a photocopy) is considered acceptable when the following conditions are met: The medical certificate is signed (with a handwritten, electronic or stamped signature) and completed by one of the following practitioners: When the patient is in Canada, the certificate must be completed by a doctor or a nurse practitioner. When the patient is outside of Canada, the certificate must be completed by a doctor or nurse practitioner recognized by the appropriate government authority with similar qualifications to a Canadian doctor or nurse practitioner. electronic The certificate contains the following information about the doctor or nurse practitioner: name; address or the address of the affiliated clinic or hospital; telephone number; license or registration number. Except for the signature, not all of the information needed to identify the doctor or nurse practitioner must appear on the medical certificate. When the doctor or nurse practitioner can be identified by the information provided, the medical certificate is considered valid. This does not apply to a doctor or nurse practitioner who is outside of Canada. The medical certificate also contains the following information about the doctor or nurse practitioner who is outside of Canada: name of the university where the diploma was obtained; the year the diploma was obtained; the city and country where the diploma was obtained; the organization that oversees the licence; proof of a valid licence or a website where it can be verified; confirmation they have the legal authority in their country of practice to make diagnoses, order and interpret tests, prescribe medications and treat the critically ill patient referenced in the medical certificate. Verifying medical credentials When there is doubt about the authenticity of the doctor or nurse practitioner’s credentials, the officer verifies if that person is licensed to practise medicine in Canada. To do this, the officer inputs the doctor’s or nurse practitioner’s license number or name in the Canadian medical regulatory authority website of the province in which the patient is receiving medical care. To verify the doctor’s or nurse practitioner’s credentials, the officer refers to Medical certificate: Medical and dental regulatory authorities — Knowledge . Medical certificate: Medical and dental regulatory authorities — Knowledge Determining if an electronic signature is acceptable Acceptable forms of electronic signatures include, but are not limited to, the following: a simple electronic signature, which is a name drawn by typing or using the mouse and includes a Read and approved seal, which is displayed directly above the signature block. an advanced or qualified digital signature, which is a document signed with a digital certificate issued by a certification authority and then cryptographically sealed. a scanned handwritten signature, or an ink stamp on which the signature is engraved and can be uploaded electronically. The signature stamp itself does not need to include the doctor’s or other medical professional’s license number. When the client starts the electronic application, ACP interfaces with the mainframe in order to determine if a previous benefit period (BP) exists and, if so, whether it is renewable. Depending on the claim data found, the client is presented with either the initial or renewal application for benefits. When ACP cannot determine whether renewability is an option at the onset of the application, the long form of the application is presented. The long form of the initial application and of the renewal application includes questions that are unique to each. benefit period If ACP determines that a previous BP is renewable, it assigns a renewal registration number and attempts to renew the claim. If unable to automate the renewal, ACP creates a CA Renewal WI. It is rare (i.e. an anomaly) for ACP to assign an initial registration number or create a CA Initial WI when there is a renewable claim. One scenario where a claim may be registered as initial, but should be a renewal is when the client applies more than 4 weeks after the last renewable week of the previous claim. In such cases, if ACP is unable to automate the claim, an initial registration number is assigned and a CA WI created. If the client then requests an antedate for a week that falls within the preceding BP and the antedate is allowed, the claim is processed as a renewal. It is also possible that an officer actioning a Claim Setup (CS) WI or registering a paper application might incorrectly assign an initial registration number or terminate the previous claim when inputting an Initial Intake (M149) transaction. Unless there is documentation indicating that the client has opted to start a new claim (the officer refers to Terminating a benefit period ), an application for benefits must always be processed as a renewal when a previous claim has a week or more remaining that is payable (the officer refers to Maximum entitlement to benefits ). Employers can provide a SUB plan to supplement EI benefits paid during periods of unemployment. To be entitled to the SUB payment, a client must be receiving EI benefits the same week (excluding the WP if this period is part of the plan). Before issuing a SUB payment, the employer (or the administrator of an approved plan) is responsible for verifying that the client is receiving EI benefits. The employer refers to a Service Canada system-generated SUB report or benefit statements submitted by the client to the employer. When a week is processed in MPS, the Service Canada system does not generate a SUB report. If the SUB code in FTS is 10 - Approved and listing issued to employer and a week of regular, sickness, WS or training benefits is processed, the IPOC officer creates and sends an ACS letter to the employer detailing the client’s EI payments. If a week of maternity benefits, parental benefits, CCB or FCB is processed, the IPOC officer does not create an ACS letter.

Some payments contain a third party recoupment (e.g. a family order agreement [FOA], an assignment of benefits [AOB], or a Canada Revenue Agency [CRA] set-off). When cancelling such payments, the officer cannot remove the portion of the payment that has been sent to the third party from the client’s payment history on the claim or tax file. Because those departments have already received payment from ESDC, the recoupment cannot be reversed when the client’s portion of the payment is returned. If the client is not entitled to the payment, the IPOC officer establishes an OP equal to the amount recouped from the original payment. If the payment was returned as undeliverable, the amount recouped is not cancelled, but remains on the original payment and no OP is established.

The officer must cancel the claim and delete the application when one of the following conditions is met: The client does not provide proof of identity. The letter concerning client authentication is returned as undeliverable. Cancelling the claim and deleting the application is a 2-step process. When proof of identity is not provided by the initial bring-forward date, the officer cancels the claim. However, the application is not deleted until the date of application + 44 days. When the subsequent bring-forward date is reached, the officer reviews the file to ensure the reason for deletion is still valid. If proof of identity is on file at this date, the application is not deleted. If proof of identity is not on file at this date, the officer sends a Reminder (REM) WI to the authorized user to delete the application. Only an authorized user can delete an application.

When more than one street name for the postal code is displayed, officers must select the correct street name. To confirm a postal code, the officer must refer to the Canada Post Web site. The date the change of address takes effect determines the inputs to process. Immediate change of address When the change of address takes effect immediately or within the current week it is considered an immediate change of address. The change of address is input on a Name and Address Change / Transfer (M159) transaction. Postdated change of address A client can report a change of address before the move. If the client reports a change of address more than a week in advance but within 180 days of the move, the change of address is considered a post-dated change of address. The change of address is input on a Post-Dated Change of Address (M259) transaction. If the client reports a change of address that occurs more than 180 days before the move, the client is advised to contact the call centre within 180 days of the move.

Undeliverable mail is any kind of mail returned to the processing centre because the address is incomplete or the client does not live or no longer lives at that address. There are 2 kinds of undeliverable documents: a Notice of Debt and other undeliverable mail. Notices of Debt are issued to inform clients that a new account has been created (overpayment or penalty). Undeliverable mail is any document (letter, annex, questionnaire, etc.), other than a Notice of Debt, returned undelivered. Depending on the situation, the officer must ensure that necessary actions regarding any undeliverable mail are taken. When processing a change of address, one of the following indicators that undeliverable mail has been received may be on file: The undeliverable mail indicator ($) displayed before the address is used when an undeliverable Notice of Debt is received by the Canada Revenue Agency. The 48 - Moved - address unknown disentitlement (D48) is imposed when mail is returned to the processing center as undeliverable. The 48 - Stop payment due to undeliverable mail stop payment (MA48) is imposed on active claims when any mail sent by Integrity is returned undeliverable, regardless of the BPC under review. An MA48 may also be imposed when a cheque is returned to IPOC as undeliverable. For further information on how to process an undeliverable Notice of Debt, the officer must refer to Undeliverable Notice of Debt . All paper and electronic ROEs in RCM that were issued with the old SIN and used to calculate the claim must be re-entered as interim ROEs with the new SIN. This applies to both paper and electronic ROEs. In addition, the processing officer documents the SIN change under both the new and old SIN and submits the information to IPOC using an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction . An IPOC officer then takes all the required actions related to the SIN change on any continuing, renewal, or dormant claims. interim ROEs The processing officer ensures that all ROEs issued since the new SIN became valid have been correctly issued with the new SIN. If an employer issues an ROE with the old SIN and the new SIN is already valid, the officer deletes the ROE and asks the employer to reissue the ROE with the new SIN. In addition to creating an interim ROE, the officer creates a Reminder (REM) WI while awaiting the ROE.

When a change of address results in a claim being transferred to another region, any active direct deposit information is automatically transferred if the claim is successfully uploaded in the transfer-in region. If an active direct deposit account also exists in the new region, the active direct deposit information from the transfer-out region is assumed to be the accurate one. The active account from the transfer-out region replaces the active account from the transfer-in region. The end date for the direct deposit information in the transfer-out region is automatically modified to reflect the transfer date minus one day. Direct deposit information for the new region does not need to be modified. It can take up to 3 business days for a payment to be deposited into a client’s bank account. If a payment has just been issued, there is no need to wait to change the direct deposit information. A temporary payment reference number is assigned to payments processed in BPS until Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) sends the actual funds electronically to the client’s bank. The payment reference number appears in FTS on the Payment Summary (MN19) screen or in SPS. Temporary payment reference numbers begin with a T (e.g. T1234-56789101). Once PSPC issues the payment to the bank, it is assigned a permanent payment reference number. For direct deposit payments, the payment reference number begins with a D (e.g. D1234-56789101). A permanent payment reference number is assigned to each payment that has been issued to the bank, whether or not the payment was rejected during the attempt to deposit it into the client’s account. If no payment has a temporary payment reference number, IPOC officers actioning RPANs can modify direct deposit account information immediately in FTS. Once entered, the direct deposit information is automatically updated and does not remain under the Pending/Reject tab for overnight processing.

It can take up to 3 days for a payment to be deposited into a client’s bank account. If a payment has just been issued, there is no need to wait to end the direct deposit information. A temporary payment reference number is assigned to payments processed in BPS until Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) sends the actual funds electronically to the client’s bank. The payment reference number appears in FTS on the Payment Summary (MN19) screen or in SPS. Temporary payment reference numbers begin with a T (e.g. T1234-56789101). Once PSPC issues the payment to the bank, it is assigned a permanent payment reference number. For direct deposit payments, the permanent payment reference number begins with a D (e.g. D1234-56789101). The IPOC officer processes the change of an OP infraction code when the claim is blocked or archived. The retroactive decision could change from a misrepresentation to non-misrepresentation or vice versa but the OP is to remain on file. The IPOC officer must: review the decision and if an OP was manually calculated on the original decision, calculate the OP for the weeks in question to confirm that the OP amount posted is correct; make the changes in FTS and PSCD if the established OP is still valid and is on a blocked or archived claim; review any violations or penalties, if necessary; send the ACS letter, if necessary. On an MM06 transaction, the Integrity or processing officer informs the IPOC officer of the decision and provides the OP infraction code information and any additional claim decisions (e.g. violation, penalty, ACS letter) related to the BPC.

The IPOC officer must: review the e-ledger for the OP in question to confirm that the OP amount posted on the original decision is correct; review any violations or penalties, if necessary; send the ACS letter, if necessary. FTS If requested, the IPOC officer rescinds the violation imposed for the retroactive decision that caused the OP. If required, the IPOC officer inputs the Claimant’s Reports (T072) transaction to correct the pay history summary (PHS). The IPOC officer changes the Gross amount field to reflect the amount that is now payable because of the retroactive non-misrepresentation decision. PSCD The original occurrence date does not change. Using the Non-Financial Debt Adjust transaction, the officer changes the infraction and message codes to non-misrepresentation to reflect the new information provided on the Archived Operational Centre Memo (HM06) screen. If no payment was applied to the interest, this input reverses any interest accumulated. Once a payment is applied, that portion of the debt is cleared. If a payment has been applied to the interest, PSCD cannot automatically reverse the cleared interest. The IPOC officer receives the following error message: “The debt has been cleared or partially cleared. Changes to the Offence Code are not allowed.” The IPOC officer sends an iService request providing the new information to have the infraction and message codes changed and the interest adjusted or refunded. DARS If a debt originally established in DARS was not converted to PSCD, the IPOC officer determines if the interest accumulated in DARS must now be refunded to the client or redistributed to another EI debt. If so, the IPOC officer sends an iService request to have the interest refunded or redistributed. If a debt originally established in DARS was partially or fully converted to PSCD, the outstanding principle and interest balances are converted separately. The principle has a document type of ES - Establishment and the interest has a document type of IN - Interest . The Origin field displays 3A - Document from Migration for both document types. The IPOC officer inputs the Non-Financial Debt Adjust transaction to change the infraction and message codes to non-misrepresentation. PSCD attempts to reverse the interest it posted, but cannot reverse the converted interest. The IPOC officer receives an error message stating that the converted interest cannot be reversed. Then, the IPOC officer determines if there is any interest in DARS. If so, the IPOC officer sends an iService request to have the interest adjusted or refunded. If requested, the IPOC officer rescinds the penalty imposed for the retroactive decision. This input also reverses the payments applied to the penalty and the credit is applied to another outstanding OP balance. If no other OP balance exists, a credit refund is issued to the client. MPS e-ledger If required, the IPOC officer enters amended (MA19) trailers on the TC85 tab to show the actual Gross benefit (PHS) that is now payable because of the retroactive non-misrepresentation decision. On the Notes tab, the IPOC officer inputs an alert to advise that the PHS must be verified once the claim is terminated. For more information, the IPOC officer must refer to Terminating an active MPS claim . Terminating an active MPS claim

If a fraudulent application is received on a continuing claim, the officer determines if the initial claim in FTS is legitimate. The officer then verifies in FTS if the client’s address and direct deposit information has been changed on the legitimate continuing claim: If yes, the officer considers the claim as compromised and imposes an MA71. If no, the officer considers the claim as not compromised. No MA71 is required and the officer sends an AI WI to Integrity for investigation. This ensures that the MA71 does not penalize the true SIN holder on the legitimate claim, since the claim has not been compromised.

To determine the tentative BPC, the last day worked (LDW) that the client declared on the application is compared with the date on which the application was submitted. If the application was submitted within the 4 calendar weeks following the week in which the LDW occurred, the tentative BPC is based on the LDW. If the LDW was a Sunday, Monday or Tuesday, the tentative BPC is the client’s last week worked. If the LDW was a Wednesday, Thursday, Friday or Saturday, the tentative BPC is the week after the client’s last week worked. If the application was submitted more than 4 calendar weeks following the week in which the last day of work occurred, the tentative BPC is the week in which the application was submitted. Example

To determine the tentative BPC, the last day of work declared by the client on the application is compared with the date that the application was submitted. If the application was submitted within the 4 calendar weeks following the week in which the last day of work occurred, the tentative BPC is based on the last day worked. If the last day of work was a Sunday, Monday or Tuesday, the tentative BPC is the client’s last week worked. If the last day of work was a Wednesday, Thursday, Friday or Saturday, the tentative BPC is the week after the client’s last week worked. If the application was submitted more than 4 calendar weeks following the week in which the last day of work occurred, the tentative BPC is the week the application was submitted.

Fraudulent paper ROEs were created fraudulently without the knowledge of the real SIN-holder and the employer associated with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number (BN) indicated in block 5 of the ROE. There are also instances where there are reasons to suspect that the business identified on the ROE is illegitimate or suspicious and was created to issue fraudulent ROEs. These fraudulent ROEs were sent to Service Canada and scanned as documents in support of fraudulent EI applications or uploaded in AppliWeb or MSCA. A close examination may reveal a difference in the font and size of the characters in the serial number of these ROEs when compared to the normal format. In some cases, RCM validates the serial number and does not signal the ROE as a duplicate, because that serial number was used to establish an EI Claim more than 11 years ago. In other situations, the serial number has been issued within the last 11 years to a different business number than the one used on the fraudulent ROE, however RCM validates the serial number but does not flag it as a duplicate because the ROE was never used to establish a claim. When correcting an ROE, the officer can detect a potentially fraudulent ROE even if no error message is displayed regarding the status of the serial number. Officers actioning the ROE Correction WI do not fact-find with the employer. Officers delete the ROE in RCM, suspend the application process and refer the file to Integrity, if the file is not already under investigation. For more information, officers refer to Fraud indicators: Identifying potentially fraudulent claims — Knowledge . Fraud indicators: Identifying potentially fraudulent claims — Knowledge

Even if the information on the ROE matches the information on the application, this does not mean that the application is authentic. Fraudulent ROEs can be paper, ROE Web or ROE SAT. Fraudulent paper ROEs were created without the knowledge of the true SIN-holder and the employer associated with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number (BN) indicated in block 5 of the ROE. There are also instances where there are reasons to suspect that the business identified on the ROE is illegitimate or suspicious and was created to issue fraudulent ROEs. These fraudulent ROEs were sent to Service Canada and scanned as documents in support of fraudulent applications for benefits, or uploaded in AW or MSCA. A close examination may reveal a difference in the font and size of the characters in the serial number of these ROEs when compared to the normal format. In some cases, RCM validates the serial number and does not signal the ROE as a duplicate, because that serial number was used to establish an EI claim more than 11 years ago. In other situations, the serial number has been issued within the last 11 years to a different business number than the one used on the fraudulent ROE, however, RCM validates the serial number but does not flag it as a duplicate because the ROE was never used to establish an EI claim. When a suspicious business is identified, an Integrity officer changes the status of suspicious employers to Under investigation in RMDS, and changes the status of any associated ROEs to Stolen . Then, a SROC is automatically created in NWS for the associated application, indicating that the claim is under investigation. When entering an ROE that has been marked as stolen, a message is displayed indicating that there is a problem with the status of the serial number. The Non-complex officer follows normal procedures and submits the ROE with the error, which creates an ROE Issue (ROE) Correction WI. When entering an ROE (paper, scanned or uploaded), the officer may suspect that an ROE is fraudulent even if no error message is displayed about the status of the serial number. Before entering the ROE in RCM, the officer suspends the application process, if necessary, and refers the file to Integrity, if the file is not already under investigation. If no fact-finding is required, the officer follows normal procedures and enters the ROE. Once the ROE is entered in RCM, the officer deletes the ROE. When an ROE RFS Action WI is received and a link has not yet been created between the ROE and a period of employment, the Non-complex agent must review the applicable ROE in RCM and the periods of employment listed in NWS. The Non-complex agent determines if one of the periods of employment listed in NWS matches the employer’s name on the ROE. Variations in the employer’s name Minor spelling differences between the employer’s name on the ROE and the period of employment are accepted. The agent must also consider that the employer may do business under more than one name. For example, the ROE indicates that the employer’s name is 123456 ONT Inc., but the client reported working for ABC Company. If the documentation on file or the Employer search (by business number) in FTS indicates that 123456 ONT Inc. operates as ABC Company, the names are equivalent and considered to be a match. Reviewing the dates on the ROE Only one ROE can be matched to each period of employment listed in NWS. The agent must review the Search / Correct - Results screen in RCM to determine if the ROE in the ROE RFS Action WI is the one with the last day for which paid (LDP) closest to the last day worked (LDW) for one of the periods of employment. The agent creates a link between the ROE and the period of employment with the matching employer’s name and best match for LDP and LDW. If either the employer’s name does not match or the LDP and LDW are not a good match, the agent does not create a link between the ROE and the period of employment. More than one ROE for one period of employment There may be more than one ROE but only one period of employment for the same employer. Example 1 Period of employment information declared on application: Callout Search / Correct - Results in RCM: ROE RFS Action WI #1 for W12345678 The agent completes the period of employment information section as follows: Matching POE : Select ABC Company . ROE RFS Action WI #2 for W12341234 The agent completes the period of employment information section as follows: Matching POE : Select POE not in the list . There may also be more than one period of employment for the same employer. Example 2 Period of employment information declared on application: Callout Callout Search / Correct - Results in RCM: ROE RFS Action WI #1 for W12345678 The agent completes the period of employment information section as follows: Matching POE : Select ABC Company (LDW 30/11/2015). ROE RFS Action WI #2 for W12341234 The agent completes the period of employment information section as follows: Matching POE : Select ABC Company (LDW 30/07/2015). ROE already linked If the ROE is linked to a period of employment with a corresponding electronic record of decision (ROD) or an outstanding Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI, the ROE RFS Action WI is completed without further action by the Non-complex agent.

Before contacting clients to validate their identity, officers determine if the application is already under investigation for potential fraud. Officers can determine that there is an ongoing Integrity investigation for this application if: a 71 - Integrity Services case manual action (MA71) or 71 - Integrity services case disentitlement (D71) is imposed; an SROC created by Integrity is on file; an Action Item (AI) is assigned to Integrity; a Call Back (CB) is assigned to Integrity. If none of these is on the file, officers review the file to determine if fraud indicators are present. If yes, officers: impose D71 on skeleton and BPNE 1, 2 or 7 claims or an MA71 on established claims, when required; complete the registration number to suspend the application process to prevent the claim from establishing or to prevent payments on the renewal claim until an investigation is completed; refer the issue to Integrity for investigation. For more information, officers refer to Referral to Integrity: Temporary measures and fraudulent EI and EI ERB claims —Instructions . Ever since the identity program was introduced in 1976, clients must prove their identity when applying for a SIN. There are blank fields in the SIR for clients with SINs issued before 1976 who have not since confirmed their identity. Blank fields in the SIR prevent the application from being validated electronically. The application cannot be accepted until the client’s identity is validated. When there are blank fields in the SIR database, the officer cannot validate the client’s identity by telephone. If the client has previously submitted an application and the proof of identity was obtained for the same non-match element, the officer can accept an SROC on the last application. Otherwise, the client must go to a Service Canada centre (SCC) or submit their proof of identity by mail or online.

An automated decision cannot be made when clients report referred training on an electronic training questionnaire completed in AW, IRS or MSCA. In this situation, ACP determines that a Level 1 decision is required and does the following: When the electronic questionnaire is submitted through AW and the application is registered as an initial claim by ACP, an Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI is created. When the electronic questionnaire is submitted through IRS or MSCA and an initial decision is outstanding, an ADJ WI is created. Another registration number is not obtained. This applies to claims in the automation process and to those with an outstanding Claim Assessment (CA) WI or Specialized Application (SA) WI. In addition, when the electronic questionnaire is submitted through IRS, the claimant’s report creates a trip-down (the claimant’s report is not processed and the client is told to call in to have the claimant’s report completed).

When converting a continuing claim, a client may report a new contentious issue (e.g. RFS, farming or availability) that must be adjudicated. If there is no existing WI for this issue, the Level 1 officer creates a CR WI for each contentious issue and attempts to adjudicate the issue according to the National Policy on Levels of Decision . If it is not possible to adjudicate the issue at Level 1, the Level 1 officer reassigns the CR WI for the contentious issue to Level 2 for adjudication. The Level 1 officer completes the conversion inputs and imposes a 1 - General suspension of benefits (stop payment) manual action (MA1) to prevent payment of benefits until the contentious issue is adjudicated. National Policy on Levels of Decision

Clients are entitled to sickness benefits if they submit proof of their own illness, injury or quarantine. The client can receive up to 26 weeks of sickness benefits per benefit period (BP) for a BPC in w/c 2374 or later, and up to 15 weeks of sickness benefits per BP for a BPC in w/c 2373 or earlier. Once a claim has been established, a client can receive a combination of regular and special benefits within the BP. The maximum entitlement to benefits varies based on the BT received. The maximum number of weeks payable for each BT cannot be exceeded. maximum entitlement to benefits Note The officer imposes a 22 - Illness (maximum sickness/special benefits paid) disentitlement (D22) when a client requests sickness benefits but the maximum weeks of sickness benefits have already been paid. Note

To allow the payment of sickness benefits, the officer must determine the period for which the client is incapable of working. This is done by determining the following information: the incapacity start date the end date of the incapacity the expected recovery date the recovery week to be input Incapacity start date For a conversion from CCB to sickness benefits on a continuing claim, the incapacity start date indicated on the medical certificate is the accepted date. If the medical certificate does not specify a start date, the officer accepts the earliest of the following as the incapacity start date: the Sunday of the week the doctor signed the medical certificate; the Sunday of the week of the medical consultation. If the medical certificate does not specify a start date, the officer accepts the doctor’s signature date or the date the doctor saw the client as the incapacity start date. If the certificate does not contain any of these dates, the officer contacts and asks the client to submit a new medical certificate with the incapacity start date. If the client does not submit a new medical certificate, the officer imposes a D16. Incapacity end date The incapacity end date is the last day the client is incapable of working. The period of incapacity ends the day before the recovery date. Recovery date The recovery date is the first day the client is capable of working. The medical certificate is used to determine the recovery date. Recovery week The recovery week is the week up to which sickness benefits are payable. To determine the recovery week, the officer refers to Determining the recovery week — Instructions . Determining the recovery week — Instructions

If there is an outstanding disentitlement on the claim, the disentitlement must be reviewed to determine if it still applies. A Level 1 officer can terminate or rescind the disentitlement if it meets the conditions specified in the National Policy on Levels of Decision . If the information on file allows for the disentitlement to be terminated, the disentitlement ends on the Friday of the week before the conversion week. National Policy on Levels of Decision The Level 1 officer can render the decision to terminate a disentitlement on a CCB claim and allow sickness benefits to be paid on a continuing or renewal claim when all of the following conditions are met: The client is requesting a conversion from compassionate care benefits to sickness benefits. There is a 51 - Does not meet compassionate care entitlement conditions disentitlement (D51), a 52 - Compassionate care benefits exhausted disentitlement (D52), or a 53 - Compassionate care benefits - No medical proof disentitlement (D53) on file. The client is requesting the conversion to sickness benefits after the end of the period for which CCB was requested. The client meets the entitlement conditions for sickness benefits requested. There is no disentitlement on file related to not otherwise available, self-employment or a labour dispute. The reason for not returning to work can be allowed at Level 1 and is related to the BT requested. If the outstanding disentitlement is a 15 - Claim procedure disentitlement (D15) imposed by Integrity and related to a missed client information session, the Level 1 officer refers the D15 issue to Level 2. If Integrity imposed the D15 for any other reason, the Level 1 officer always refers the D15 issue to Integrity. For more information, the officer refers to Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity . Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity Based on the letter that was sent, the officer can determine the reason the D15 is imposed: For client information sessions, a letter beginning with C-73 is sent. For direction to report to a fact-finding interview or to reply to a request for information, a letter beginning with C-72 or C-88 is sent.

The Claim action status Renewal is created when a renewal decision is registered. There are 3 Claim action statuses that may be displayed: In Progress (Automation) is displayed on the Client information tree when there are one or more outstanding adjudication issues. In Progress (Manual) is displayed on the Client information tree when there is no outstanding adjudication issue and there is an outstanding CA or Specialized Application (SA) WI. Finalized is displayed on the Client information tree when all ADJ WIs are completed and the renewal week has been successfully input. An ADJ WI is created for every new contentious issue. When opening an ADJ WI, the officer must always check to see if there is a Resolve Issue tab. If there is a Resolve Issue tab, the officer can document the decision directly in the ADJ WI by completing all mandatory screens. When the ADJ WI is completed, NWS creates a record of decision (ROD) based on the Resolve Issue screens. When the renewal is finalized, the system also generates the required transactions (e.g. signature code, disentitlement) based on the Resolve Issue screens. If a disentitlement or indefinite disqualification is imposed, the system creates a Correspondence (COR) WI for the D-01-00-00 letter. This means that the officer with the CA or SA WI has no action to perform for these ADJ WIs. If there is no Resolve Issue tab for the ADJ WI, the officer must create a ROD, generate the required transactions and send the appropriate letter. If there is an outstanding CA or SA WI when the officer completes the ADJ WI, a client Note is created and the officer with the CA or SA WI must follow the instructions to input the transactions or send the letter.

A client does not have to collect all of the weeks of parental benefits successively. The payment of parental benefits can occur in one benefit period (BP) or over 2 BPs, as long as the maximum number of parental weeks is not exceeded and the end of the PW has not been reached.

If there is an outstanding disentitlement on the claim, the disentitlement must be reviewed to determine if it still applies to the renewal (conversion). A Level 1 officer can terminate or rescind the disentitlement if it meets the conditions specified in the National Policy on Levels of Decision . If the information on file allows for the disentitlement to be terminated, it is terminated on the Friday of the week before the renewal (conversion) week. National Policy on Levels of Decision If the outstanding disentitlement is a 15 - Claim procedure disentitlement (D15) imposed by Integrity and related to a missed client information session, the Level 1 officer refers the D15 issue to Level 2. If Integrity imposed the D15 for any other reason, the Level 1 officer always refers the D15 issue to Integrity. For more information, the officer refers to Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity . Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity Based on the letter that was sent, the officer can determine the reason the D15 is imposed: For client information sessions, a letter beginning with C-73 is sent. For direction to report to a fact-finding interview or to reply to a request for information, a letter beginning with C-72 or C-88 is sent.

Quebec region Clients who live in Quebec and who request benefits due to a pregnancy, birth or adoption must apply to QPIP . The Quebec government pays these benefits to Quebec residents. In some cases, the Quebec government also pays QPIP benefits to a parent living outside of Quebec if both parents lived in Quebec when the initial claim for maternity or parental benefits for the birth or adoption of the same child was made. When a client applying for EI benefits lives in Quebec or indicates that the other parent is entitled to QPIP benefits, the officer on the specialized team that is responsible for liaising with QPIP determines whether the client is entitled to the requested EI benefits. QPIP When a client living in Quebec is entitled to receive QPIP, an officer from the specialized QPIP team imposes an indefinite 57 - E.I. Maternity or Parental benefits denied, benefits are payable by the province disentitlement (D57).

Parents can share parental benefits. For more information and definitions, the officer refers to Parents: Definition — Table . Parents: Definition — Table The type of parental benefits requested by the first parent to apply determines the type of parental benefits all parents are entitled to receive for the same birth, adoption or placement, regardless of which parent is paid first. When fact-finding with parents who applied for benefits after the first parent, the officer informs the other parents of this. Once at least one week of parental benefits has been paid to any parent, all parents requesting parental benefits for the same birth, adoption or placement are only entitled to receive the type of parental benefits selected by the first parent who applied for benefits. The maximum shareable entitlement is 40 weeks of standard parental benefits or 69 weeks of extended parental benefits for children born or placed for adoption on or after March 17, 2019. For children born or placed for adoption before this date, the maximum shareable entitlement is 35 weeks of standard parental benefits or 61 weeks of extended parental benefits. The maximum entitlement for one client remains at 35 weeks of standard or 61 weeks of extended benefits. Clients can change the number of weeks that each parent receives at any time before all benefits are paid. When clients cannot agree on the number of weeks they will each receive, the officer reassigns the issue to a Level 2 officer who adjudicates the division of the remaining weeks. Clients who apply for parental benefits must provide the name and SIN of the other parent for control purposes. If the client does not provide the name and the SIN of the other parent, or in the case of a single parent or a parent whose family situation is such that information on the child’s other parent cannot be obtained, the officer can still allow the claim Validating shared parental benefits A Parental Client Record is created for every client requesting parental benefits. The Parental Client Record consists of the client’s SIN, the arrival or placement week (APW) and the other parent’s SIN, if it has been provided. Once a claim is finalized, the system links Parental Client Records for all clients who are sharing parental benefits for the same child. The Parental sharing validation process creates a Claim Review (CR) Parental Benefits Validation WI when one of the following conditions is met: The parental benefit type on all linked Parental Client Records is not the same. The total number of parental weeks requested on all linked Parental Client Records exceeds the maximum number of shareable parental benefit weeks. FTS The officer inputs the other parent’s SIN using the Parental Benefits Validation transaction in the Enquiry menu in FTS. This screen also displays linked parents’ SINs and the associated APW. Note Note Other parent’s SIN When the client has provided the other parent’s SIN, the officer manually enters it on the day following the parental input. Note If the client’s SIN has already been linked to the other parent, no entry is necessary.

Communication of the renewal decision is not necessary when the only transaction input is the renewal transaction. When another decision is input at the time of the renewal (disentitlement, disqualification or allocation of earnings), communication of the decision is necessary. Written communication of the decision is usually done by officers who are responsible for sending the appropriate letter. In certain situations, the R-01-00-00 letter is sent automatically. Officers must ensure that the letter was sent and, if it was not sent, they must create and send the letter of decision in ACS. If a renewal and an allocation are input by the same officer and are processed on the same day, the R-01-00-00 letter is, in most cases, created automatically. However, the letter is not sent automatically if one of the following conditions is met: One of the transactions (M106 or M175) rejects. The allocation code on the M175 is A , D , or N . An E or W allocation is input for more than one week. A stop payment is imposed (MA01, MA02, MA48, MA71, MA72, MA73, MA74, MA75). A disqualification or disentitlement is being input. A disqualification or disentitlement is already on file and is not being rescinded or terminated. In some cases, the letter may be sent automatically but additional decisions must be communicated. To prevent duplication of letters, the officer must prevent the letter from being sent automatically by using the Automated Letter Bypass function in FTS.

Renewal advantages When assessing a renewal, it might be to the client’s advantage to establish a new BP instead of renewing the existing BP. The officer must refer to Cancelling, voiding, terminating or withdrawing a claim for more information. Cancelling, voiding, terminating or withdrawing a claim Subsequent claim The renewal application can be used to establish a subsequent claim when the following conditions are met: The claim is renewed and there are 4 or fewer weeks of benefits remaining in the BP. The client has worked enough hours to establish a new claim. ACP can register the subsequent claim if the Claim Assessment (CA) WI for a renewal or subsequent initial claim is finalized within 28 days of the renewal application. When ACP cannot register the subsequent claim because the renewal is not processed within 28 days of the renewal application (i.e. REN WK not found or no match and polling limit exceeded is displayed on the Processing Activities tab in NWS) or when the claim was converted to MPS, the officer processing the CA Renewal WI creates a Reminder (REM) WI. This ensures that an officer will manually register the subsequent claim. Adjudicating new contentious issues When renewing a claim, a client may report a new contentious issue (e.g. RFS, farming or availability) that must be adjudicated. If the issue is reported on the application, the system creates an Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI. If a contentious issue is detected while reviewing the claim, the Level 1 officer must create an ADJ WI for each contentious issue and must attempt to adjudicate the issue according to the National Policy on Levels of Decision . If the Level 1 officer cannot adjudicate the issue, the ADJ WI is referred to Level 2 for adjudication. When an ADJ WI is created on a renewal claim, either manually or by the system, the system automatically imposes an 2 - Contentious Renewal in Automation manual action (MA2) to prevent payment of benefits until the contentious issue is adjudicated. When the renewal or a decision must be input manually, the inputs must be done before the CA WI is completed, as the completion of the WI triggers the removal of the MA2 by the system if there is no outstanding ADJ WIs. An officer cannot rescind an MA2. National Policy on Levels of Decision

Processing claimant’s reports The last week of maternity benefits must be paid before the officer can input the conversion transactions. If claimant’s reports have not yet been processed for the maternity benefits period, they must be processed before inputting the conversion. This requires a 2-day input. Previously deferred adjudication on reasons for separation (RFSs) After converting a claim to regular benefits, any RFS for which adjudication had previously been deferred must be adjudicated. When the claim is calculated, if the RFS adjudication is deferred, a disqualification is automatically imposed and appears in FTS on the Disqualification/Disentitlement screen. The officer always verifies if any contentious RFS was adjudicated by checking for a record of decision (ROD) in NWS. When actioning the renewal, the officer reviews all documentation in the electronic claim to ensure all issues and information have been addressed as appropriate. The system does not generate a new WI or send a notification for outstanding Claim Assessment (CA) or Specialized Application (SA) WIs when documents are uploaded in all situations. Renewal advantages When assessing a renewal, it might be to the client’s advantage to establish a new BP instead of renewing the existing BP. The officer must refer to Cancelling, voiding, terminating or withdrawing a claim for more information. Cancelling, voiding, terminating or withdrawing a claim Subsequent claim The renewal application can be used to establish a subsequent claim when the following conditions are met: The claim is renewed and there are 4 or fewer weeks of benefits remaining in the BP. The client has worked enough hours to establish a new claim. ACP can register the subsequent claim if the CA WI for a renewal or subsequent initial claim is finalized within 28 days of the renewal application. When ACP cannot register the subsequent claim because the renewal is not processed within 28 days of the renewal application (i.e. REN WK not found or No match and polling limit exceeded is displayed on the Processing Activities tab in NWS) or when the claim was converted to MPS, the officer processing the CA Renewal WI creates a Reminder (REM) WI. This ensures that an officer will manually register the subsequent claim. Adjudicating new contentious issues When renewing a claim, a client may report a new contentious issue (e.g. RFS, farming or availability) that must be adjudicated. If the issue is reported on the application, the system creates an Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI. If a contentious issue is detected while reviewing the claim, the Level 1 officer must create an ADJ WI for each contentious issue and must attempt to adjudicate the issue according to the National Policy on Levels of Decision . When an ADJ WI is created on a renewal claim, either manually or by the system, the system automatically imposes an 2 - Contentious Renewal in Automation manual action (MA2) to prevent payment of benefits until the contentious issue is adjudicated. When the renewal or a decision must be input manually, the inputs must be done before the CA WI is completed, as the completion of the WI triggers the removal of the MA2 by the system if there is no outstanding ADJ WIs. An officer cannot remove an MA2. National Policy on Levels of Decision

As part of Budget 2021, the Government of Canada announced that a national CER of 420 hours of insurable employment applies to establish a claim for regular or special benefits. If the client has a violation on file, the increased entrance requirements may apply. The CER applies to claims with a BPC between September 26, 2021 (w/c 2310), and September 18, 2022 (w/c 2361). During this period, the definitions for major attached and minor attached clients in EIA 6(1) are repealed. Clients whose claims are established with 420 hours of insurable employment qualify for special benefits regardless of the conversion date. The officer ensures that all other qualifying and entitlement conditions are met. increased entrance requirements During this period, the officer does not use the claim type (CT) 9 - Sickness - minor attached .

All foreign workers are given temporary resident status for a limited period of time when they enter Canada. Generally, foreign workers can demonstrate availability to accept work only if they possess a valid work permit which allows them to work in Canada. Therefore, when a foreign worker wishes to renew or convert a claim to sickness benefits, the validity of the work permit will need to be checked as the client could be deemed not otherwise available.

All foreign workers are given temporary resident status for a limited period of time when they enter Canada. Generally, foreign workers can demonstrate availability to accept work only if they possess a valid work permit which allows them to work in Canada. Maternity, parental, CCB and family caregiver benefits can be paid to clients who qualify to receive these benefits, even if their SIN has expired, under the following 3 conditions: The clients’ SINs are valid during the qualifying period (QP); The clients are authorized to be in Canada (e.g. hold a visitor or study permit or a Refugee Protection Claimant Document); The clients remain in Canada (i.e. there is no information on the claim indicating that the client is or will be out of Canada). Foreign clients applying for maternity, parental, CCB and family caregiver benefits do not need to prove their availability, so a work permit or valid SIN is not necessary during the BP. In these situations, the officer reviews the client’s authorization to remain in Canada. If a client whose SIN has expired leaves the country, the client is disentitled from receiving maternity, parental, CCB and family caregiver benefits.

Maternity benefits are available to people who are pregnant or have given birth. Maternity benefits provide income support during a leave due to a pregnancy or childbirth and can be paid up to 12 weeks before the expected DOB. Clients who want to receive parental benefits immediately after maternity benefits can apply for maternity and parental benefits at the same time. This allows the system to automatically convert the claim to parental benefits immediately after the maternity benefits are paid in full or the maternity end week is reached. If necessary, the system splits the last claimant’s report and continues to pay benefits without any interruption. When maternity benefits are paid in full or the maternity end week is reached, the system automatically changes the sex code to 8 and displays both the exact parental start week and the parental end week. If the client completes both forms at the same time but there is an interruption between the 2 types of benefits, ignore the date provided by the client and process the claims simultaneously. If the client requests to modify the start date of maternity benefits, before converting the claim, the officer must determine the impact a modification would have on the claim and communicates with the client to explain the impact on the claim.

The maternity window is defined as the period in which maternity benefits are payable. It starts on the earlier of the following dates: 12 weeks before the expected DOB (expected DOB – 12 weeks) the actual DOB. Note The maternity window ends on the latter of the following dates: 17 weeks after the expected DOB (expected DOB + 17 weeks) 17 weeks after the actual DOB (actual DOB + 17 weeks). To provide the client with the most advantageous maternity window, the actual DOB must be provided as soon as possible after the birth. The expected or actual DOB can be used to determine the period during which maternity benefits are payable. The expected or actual DOB is input on the Renewal/Revised (M106) transaction at the same time as the data required to establish the maternity claim. Actual date of birth (DOB) provided If the client provides both the expected DOB and the actual DOB, the officer determines which date will provide the longest maternity window for the client and enters it in the Confinement field during the conversion. Extending the maternity window To allow the client more time to collect maternity benefits to which they are entitled, the maternity window can be extended by one week for each week that a newborn is hospitalized within that period. The maximum extension of the maternity window is 52 weeks after the actual DOB (actual DOB + 52 weeks). The number of weeks of maternity entitlement remains the same. The officer extends the maternity window by inputting an external maternity end week. The officer calculates the extended maternity window by adding the number of full or partial weeks of hospitalization to the initial maternity end week.

To allow the payment of sickness benefits, the officer must determine the period in which the client is incapable of working by determining: the incapacity start date the end date of the incapacity the expected recovery date the recovery week to be input Incapacity start date For a conversion from regular to sickness benefits when no medical certificate needs to be submitted, the incapacity start date is the conversion week. The officer refers to Sickness: Incapacity start date — Table to determine if an incapacity start date is required. If yes, the incapacity start date is the Sunday of the week in which the doctor or other medical professional indicates that the client was unable to work for medical reasons. Sickness: Incapacity start date — Table If no specific incapacity start date is provided, the incapacity start date is the Sunday of whichever week is the earlier: the week the doctor or other medical professional signed the medical certificate; the week of the medical consultation. When the incapacity start date reported by the client is before the date indicated on the medical certificate, a D16 is imposed for the period of incapacity that is not covered by the medical certificate. If the incapacity start date, signature date or date of the medical consultation is not indicated, the medical certificate is not acceptable. The officer must conduct fact-finding with the client to obtain a new medical certificate that indicates the incapacity start date. Conversion requests that follow the payment of sickness benefits are established in the week following the last payment of sickness benefits if the client has made the conversion request within 3 weeks of the last week in which sickness benefits were processed (the week the last claimant’s report for sickness benefits was processed + 3). If the request is made 4 or more weeks after the week in which the last payment of sickness benefits was processed, the effective date of conversion is the week before the week the request was made, according to the automatic backdating policy. Processing claimant’s reports Before the officer can input the conversion transactions, the last week of sickness benefits must be paid. If claimant’s reports have not been processed for the sickness benefit period, they must be processed before inputting the conversion. This requires a 2-day input. Adjudicating new contentious issue When converting a continuing claim, a client may report a new contentious issue (e.g. reason for separation [RFS], farming or availability) that must be adjudicated. If there is no existing WI for this issue, the Level 1 officer creates a Claim Review (CR) WI for each contentious issue and attempts to adjudicate the issue according to the National Policy on Levels of Decision. If it is not possible to adjudicate the issue at Level 1, the Level 1 officer reassigns the CR WI for the contentious issue to Level 2 for adjudication. The Level 1 officer completes the conversion inputs and imposes a 1 - General suspension of benefits (stop payment) manual action (MA1) to prevent payment of benefits until the contentious issue is adjudicated.

Maternity benefits are available to people who are pregnant or have given birth. Maternity benefits provide income support during a leave due to a pregnancy or childbirth and can be paid up to 12 weeks before the expected DOB. A client who wants to have parental benefits immediately follow her maternity benefits can apply for maternity and parental benefits at the same time. This allows the system to automatically convert the claim to parental benefits immediately after the maternity benefits are paid in full or the maternity end week is reached. If necessary, the system splits the last claimant’s report and continues to pay benefits without any interruption. When maternity benefits are paid in full or the maternity end week is reached, the system automatically changes the sex code to 8 and displays the parental start week and the parental end week. If the client completes both forms at the same time but there is an interruption between the two types of benefits, ignore the date provided by the client and process the claims simultaneously. If the client requests to modify the start date of maternity benefits, before converting the claim , the officer must determine the impact a modification would have on the claim and communicates with the client to explain the impact on the claim.

The IPOC officer is responsible for: converting the terminated claim to MPS; taking all the necessary actions to remove the fraudulent information from the claim; cancelling returned payments or uncashed cheques adjusting the client’s tax file; issuing any missing payments to the client. When cancelling or removing the payments, the IPOC officer also removes any overpayments (OPs) that were established for the fraudulent payments from the client’s file. Removing versus cancelling payments The IPOC officer removes a fraudulent payment from the client’s file when a third party completed a fraudulent claimant’s report and received the payment, but the client is not entitled to the payment. The IPOC officer also removes the payment details from the pay history summary (PHS) and adjusts the client’s tax file for payments issued in the current tax year or amends the T4E for payments issued in a previous tax year. A payment cannot be removed if a replacement has been issued to the client in SPS. The IPOC officer cancels a fraudulent payment when a payment issued to a third party is returned in SPS or a cheque that was issued is never cashed, but the client is not entitled to the full payment. The IPOC officer cancels the payment, removes the payment details from the PHS and adjusts the client’s tax file for payments issued in the current tax year or amends the T4E for payments issued in a previous tax year. A payment cannot be cancelled if a replacement has been issued unless both the original and the replacement payments meet one of the following conditions: both payments have been returned; one of the payments has been returned and the other payment is an outstanding cheque that has never been cashed. When the MM06 indicates to cancel a returned payment or an uncashed cheque, the IPOC officer creates an IPOC REV WI to cancel the returned or uncashed payment in SPS. The IPOC officer then processes the payment cancellation in MPS. If the payment contains an EI OP recoupment, the IPOC officer establishes an OP equal to the OP recoupment amount. To keep the original data for Royal Canadian Mounted Police investigations, the IPOC officer does not remove fraudulent payments received by a third party in purge and recreate (P/R). If a payment issued to a third party is replaced to the client, and the client is not entitled to or does not want benefits, the IPOC officer establishes the OP on the client’s file and does not remove the weeks from the claim. The IPOC officer uses the OP codes indicated on the Archived Operational Centre Memo (HM06) screen. The IPOC officer manually updates the Pay History Modification (PHM1) screen to reflect the changes on the HM06 screen.

The IPOC officer is responsible for: voiding the claim; removing all weeks paid to the third party from the client’s file; cancelling returned payments and uncashed cheques; adjusting the client’s tax file for payments issued in the current tax or amending the T4E for payments; issued in a previous tax year; deleting the pay history, if necessary. When cancelling or removing the payments, the IPOC officer also removes any overpayments (OPs) that were established for the fraudulent payments from the client’s file. The IPOC officer also removes the payment details from the pay history and adjusts the client’s tax file for payments issued in the current tax year or amends the T4E for payments issued in a previous tax year. A payment cannot be removed if a replacement has been issued to the client in SPS. The processing officer is responsible for: reviewing the investigation report in NIIS; reviewing SPS or NWS to determine if payments issued to the third party have been returned in SPS; creating a record of decision (ROD); creating an MM06 for IPOC to remove the fraudulent payments from the claim, adjust the client’s tax file and cancel any returned payments or uncashed cheques. In SPS, payments processed on the same date have the same payment reference number and are considered one payment. In FTS, the processing officer reviews the Payments tab or the Payment Summary (MN19) screen to determine which weeks are paid under the same payment reference number. If payments were issued to a third party, and the client is requesting the same weeks and is entitled to the full amount, the payments are replaced in SPS. The processing officer creates and IPOC Review (IPOC REV) Payment replacement WI requesting a payment replacement in SPS. In this case, the IPOC officer does not adjust the client’s tax file for these weeks, because the client received the payment. If payments were issued to a third party and the client is requesting benefits for the same weeks, but is not entitled to the full amount (i.e. the client had earnings in those weeks), the payment cannot be replaced in SPS. The processing officer creates an MM06 for IPOC to: remove the fraudulent payments from the claim; adjust the client’s tax file; cancel any returned payments or uncashed cheques; issue the missing payments. In MPS, all weeks with the same payment reference number must be removed, and then the weeks to which the client is entitled to must be reissued. If payments were issued to a third party, and the client is requesting the same weeks and is entitled to the full amount for some weeks and a partial amount for other weeks, the processing officer creates an IPOC REV WI for the payments that can be replaced in SPS and an MM06 for the payments that cannot be replaced in SPS.

When the new claim is assessed, the client can establish a new BP in CPS or renew the existing BP in MPS to receive benefits during the remainder of the WS agreement.

In order to terminate the EI ERB claim, the client must be able to qualify for a new benefit period (BP) for CCB (600 hours of insurable employment). On top of the hours accumulated after the start of the EI ERB claim, the agent uses the hours before the BPC of the EI ERB claim to determine if the client qualifies for a new claim. Credit of insurable hours of employment for BPNE claims If a client requesting CCB after receiving EI ERB or CERB has fewer than 600 hours of insurable employment in their qualifying period, a credit of 480 hours is awarded to the client. The agent must create an interim ROE as follows: Block 4: EI ERB initiative – Credit hours Block 6: Weekly Block 8: Social Insurance Number Block 10: the Sunday of the EI ERB BPC Block 11: the Saturday of the last week of EI ERB Block 12: the Saturday of the last week prior of EI ERB Block 15A: 480 Block 15B: 1 Block 16: A-Shortage of work If the client still does not qualify for a new claim for CCB after the credit is awarded, the client continues to receive EI ERB or CERB for the remainder of the entitlement weeks (a maximum of 28 weeks or until October 3, 2020).

In some cases, the QP can be extended by a maximum of 52 weeks (for a maximum QP length of 104 weeks).The QP can never be extended beyond the BPC week of a previous claim. The agent does not take into account the EI ERB claim in the calculation of the QP extension. To account for the EI ERB or CERB period, the QP is extended: by 16 weeks if the BPC for the new initial claim is between March 15, 2020 and June 28, 2020. by 24 weeks if the BPC for the new initial claim between July 5, 2020 and August 23, 2020. by 28 weeks if the BPC for the new initial claim is on or after August 30, 2020. All clients are entitled to a QP extension, even if they did not receive the full 28 weeks of the EI ERB or CERB. The agent refers to Reviewing for a possible qualifying period extension to determine if the client is entitled to other QP extensions. Reviewing for a possible qualifying period extension Determining the cut-off date (COD) The agent needs to determine what the actual COD is. The COD is the most recent of the following dates: the date of a previous non-ERB claim; if the BPC is March 15, 2020 and June 28, 2020: the BPC of the new claim – 68 weeks – any other QP extensions; if the BPC is between July 5, 2020 and August 23, 2020: the BPC of the new claim – 76 weeks – any other QP extensions; if the BPC is on or after August 30, 2020: the BPC of the new claim – 80 weeks – any other QP extensions. This calculation takes into account the extension due to ERB as well as the normal 52-week the QP. Any additional QP extensions on file also need to be included. In SSA, the agent manually inputs the COD on the Coding Requirements screen in the Previously paid BPC field. This allows the new claim to bypass the EI ERB claim and be calculated accordingly. Note Inputting the QP extension The QP extension is input in SSA on the Extension of the Qualifying/ Benefit period annex. The agent selects t he dates to use in the extension as follows: From [BPC - 16] to [BPC – 1] From [BPC - 24] to [BPC – 1] From [BPC - 28] to [BPC – 1] The agent refers to Extending the qualifying period in SSA to input the QP extension and uses the Employment measures reason. Extending the qualifying period in SSA Note
