In some cases, the EI ERB claim may have already been converted to CCB and some weeks of EI ERB or CCB may have been processed. In these cases, IPOC intervention is required to properly establish the subsequent claim. If any weeks of CCB appear in the Payments tab in FTS, but no payments were issued, the agent creates an IPOC Review (IPOC REV) WI to remove CCB weeks from the EI ERB claim before establishing the subsequent CCB claim. Once the weeks are removed from the pay history summary (PHS), the agent establishes the subsequent claim. If the client has received the wrong type of benefits, the agent sends an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction to IPOC to terminate the old claim and establish the subsequent claim in purge and recreate (P/R). The overpayments (OP) created when clients receive the EI ERB instead of CCB are written off. The OP is still displayed in FTS but the balance is not recoverable. If the claim displays 5 - COVID-19 Automation Utility , the agent cannot register a recalculation in SSA because there is no claim to recalculate. The workaround is to register an initial claim, input the data to obtain a calculation result for the desired BPC, and send the file to IPOC on an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction.

When clients are receiving EI benefits, they must declare any payments they receive. If the payments are determined to be earnings, the agent allocates these monies. As a result, benefits paid to the client in that week may be reduced. The amounts to be deducted from benefits are regulated by the working while on claim (WWC) provisions and the provisions of Pilot Project 17. Pilot Project 17 was introduced on August 7, 2011 and ended on August 4, 2012 when the WWC provisions came into force. The WWC provisions can negatively affect the amount of benefits that clients can receive. To reduce these negative effects, some clients can choose to have the provisions of Pilot Project 17 apply to their earnings. Earnings deductions under the provisions of Pilot Project 17 Once the waiting period (WP) is served, a client’s benefits are reduced dollar for dollar when they exceed the allowable earnings threshold. The allowable earnings threshold is determined using of the following: 40% of the benefit rate if the benefit rate is $188 or more; or $75 if the benefit rate is less than $188. However, the earnings are deducted dollar for dollar for weeks before August 12, 2018 and the benefit type (BT) is sickness, maternity or self-employment (SE). Earnings deductions under the current Working While on Claim (WWC) provisions For weeks that occur before August 12, 2018 for BTs other than sickness, maternity or SE, and for weeks that occur on or after August 12, 2018 for all BTs, once the WP is served, the earnings are deducted as follows: If the earnings are less than or equal to the earnings threshold (i.e. 90% of the client’s weekly insured earnings), benefits are reduced at a rate of 50% of the client’s earnings each week. If the earnings exceed the earnings threshold, benefits are reduced by 50% of the amount equal to the earnings threshold, then by 100% for every dollar that exceeds the earnings threshold. However, the earnings are deducted dollar for dollar when one of the following conditions is met: The week occurs on or after August 12, 2018, the BT is sickness or maternity benefits, and the earnings are wage loss indemnity (WLI) or paid sick leave (PSL) from an employer registered in the Premium Reduction Program (PRP). The week occurs before August 12, 2018 and the BT is sickness, maternity or SE.

Canadian government employees who are posted outside Canada and their spouse who relocate with them are considered residents of Canada for income tax purposes. The CRA has set the tax deduction rate for Interstate claims at 25%. Clients who can prove that they are factual residents of Canada are not subject to the 25% tax rate and regular income tax rules apply. Clients are considered factual residents of Canada if: they are the spouse of a Canadian Government employee and move with their spouse to another country during the spouse’s foreign assignment; they intend to return to Canada following the assignment; and they maintain secondary residential ties with Canada (i.e. maintain a home in Canada or have a spouse or dependants who stayed in Canada). For more information on residential ties, refer to Government employees outside Canada . Government employees outside Canada As long as there is a verbal or written statement on file from the client confirming factual residency in Canada, officers in the Centre of Specialization for Interstate and Outside Canada claims are authorized to change the tax deduction on the claim. The Service Canada Centre (SCC) code in FTS is 3503 for Interstate claims and 3518 for Outside Canada claims.

Clients who can prove that they are factual residents of Canada are not subject to the 25% tax rate and regular income tax rules apply. Clients are considered factual residents of Canada if: they are the spouse of a Canadian Government employee and move with their spouse to another country during the spouse’s foreign assignment; they intend to return to Canada following the assignment; they maintain secondary residential ties with Canada (i.e. maintain a home in Canada or have a spouse or dependants who stayed in Canada). For more information on residential ties, refer to Government employees outside Canada . Government employees outside Canada As long as there is a verbal or written statement on file from the client confirming factual residency in Canada, officers in the Centre of Specialization for Interstate and Outside Canada claims are authorized to change the tax deduction on the claim. The Service Canada centre (SCC) code in FTS is 3503 for Interstate claims and 3518 for Outside Canada claims.

When there is one or more voluntary leaving or dismissal in the QP, any one of these events can prevent payment of regular benefits in the benefit period (BP). Adjudication is deferred on any contentious RFS before a disqualifying event that results in an indefinite disqualification 10 - Dismissal - misconduct proven (D10) or 11 - Voluntary leaving - Just cause not proven (D11). To determine a disqualifying event, the officer must first consider the most recent event of voluntary leaving or dismissal in the QP. The most recent event is not always equal to the last employment and can fall anywhere in the QP. If the officer determines that there is no disqualification for that event, fact-finding and adjudication are completed for the preceding voluntary leaving or dismissal in the QP. The officer continues to work in reverse chronological order until: an indefinite disqualification is imposed; the beginning of the QP is reached; or no event results in an indefinite disqualification. A request made more than 30 days after the date on which a notice of decision is received is considered a delayed request. However, the request can still be accepted if a reasonable explanation for the delay is provided. Processing a short delay Delays that do not exceed 120 days after the initial decision are considered short delays and are allowed without further fact-finding or documentation. The short delay period is considered a reasonable explanation in itself. Processing a request received between 121 and 365 days after the initial decision For delays between 121 and 365 days after the initial decision, requesters must provide a reasonable explanation for the delay and demonstrate a continued intention to request a reconsideration under EIA 112 . Each argument provided to explain the delay must be assessed individually. EIA 112 Note Processing a request received beyond 365 days and in other particular circumstances The following 3 circumstances require special consideration: More than 365 days have passed since the decision was communicated to the requester. The requester submitted another application for benefits after the decision was communicated. The requester has asked the Commission to rescind or amend the decision under EIA 111 . EIA 111 If any of these circumstances are present, the officer must first determine if the requester provided a reasonable explanation for the delay and demonstrated a continued intention to request a reconsideration under EIA 112. If these 2 conditions are not met, the delay can be denied. However, if these 2 conditions are met, the Commission must also be satisfied that the request for reconsideration on the substantive issue has a reasonable chance of success and that no prejudice would be caused to the Commission or any other interested party.

Human rights legislation in Canada prohibits mandatory retirement. Very few occupations are exempt from this legislation. Some employers may be able to demonstrate a genuine reason for mandatory retirement, but these cases are rare. In cases of mandatory retirement, clients do not voluntarily leave their employment. The separation is initiated by the employer. Consequently, a Level 2 officer must adjudicate the RFS as a dismissal and determine whether clients lost their employment due to misconduct. Normally, in the case of mandatory retirement, the facts on file support a decision of misconduct not proven. Written notice to the employer that EI benefits have been allowed is not required as there is no allegation of misconduct.

Adjudicating the last employment in the qualifying period (QP) — BPCs between w/c 2310 and w/c 2361 Budget 2021 has introduced a temporary simplification measure starting September 26, 2021. For claims with a BPC between w/c 2310 and w/c 2361, the officer will only adjudicate the last period of employment in the QP if it is contentious. If the officer allows the last RFS, all other ROEs in the QP, even if they are contentious, are used to calculate the claim. If, however, the officer does not allow the RFS on the last ROE in the QP, the claim is calculated with a disqualification. Note This new measure does not apply to fishing claims and claims from self-employed people. Instead, if clients have insurable employment in the QP with a contentious RFS and a BPC between w/c 2310 and w/c 2361 when they apply for self-employed (SE) or fishing benefits, the officer must adjudicate the contentious RFS following normal adjudication procedures. When the client declares other employers with a contentious RFS on the same application, if ACP does not allow the issue under auto-adjudication rules, the issue is automatically resolved and ACP creates a record of decision (ROD) that shows Adjudication not Required . The Special condition field on the ROE is not updated, and the ROE is included in the calculation. An Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI is not created for the RFS. ACP does not always automatically create an ADJ WI when the application is received. However, if an ROE with a contentious RFS is received during the automation process, ACP may create an ADJ WI or ROE Issue (ROE) RFS Action WI. When there is more than one ROE with the same last day paid (LDP), and one of the ROEs is contentious while the other ROE is not, adjudication is not required and both ROEs are included in the calculation. A client may find employment at the beginning of the BP and subsequently leave or lose that employment before the initial claim is established. An Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI is created for officers to adjudicate the contentious RFS. When the decision is that the client was dismissed due to misconduct and that a D10 indefinite disqualification applies in the BP, the system does not automatically impose a disqualification in the BP when the officer completes the screens on the Resolve Issue tab. When adjudicating an RFS issue in the BP of a claim for which the Claim action status is In Progress , the Level 2 officer documents the decision on the Resolve Issue tab of the ADJ WI, verbally communicates the negative decision to the client and creates a draft of the D-01-00-00 letter as normal. However, the Level 2 officer also manually inputs a D15 and creates a Reminder (REM) WI for Level 1 before completing the ADJ WI. The Level 2 officer manually imposes a D15 effective from the Monday of the week of the disqualifying event. Imposing the D15 allows the claim to continue in automation and prevents the payment of benefits from the date the client is dismissed due to misconduct in the BP. When creating the REM WI for Level 1, the Level 2 officer includes instructions to impose the indefinite D10, rescind the D15 and send the D-01-00-00 letter. The Level 1 officer waits until the claim is established before actioning the REM WI.

When there is an outstanding adjudication issue on a renewal claim, the Claim action status is In Progress (Automation) . All Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WIs must be completed before the system can finalize the renewal. There is a Resolve Issue tab for ADJ Dismissal WIs which includes screens where the officer documents the decision. When the ADJ WI is completed, the system creates a ROD based on the Resolve Issue screens. When the renewal is finalized, the system generates the required transactions based on the Resolve Issue screens and removes the stop payment (MA02). If the dismissal or suspension is allowed and the employer must be notified, the system automates the Z-01-00-00 letter, or creates a Correspondence (COR) WI. If the dismissal or suspension is not allowed, the system creates a COR WI for the D-01-00-00 or N-00-00-00 letter. A temporary Budget 2021 measure applies to claims with a BPC between September 26, 2021 (w/c 2310) and September 18, 2022 (w/c 2361). During this period, adjudication is required only if the RFS on the most recent ROE in the QP is contentious. In addition, the officer does not use the common entrance requirement (CER) of 420 hours of insurable employment to determine if the client requalifies after a disqualifying event. Instead, the client needs to have worked at least one hour in insurable employment since the disqualifying event and to have filed an EI application. If the RFS since the disqualifying event on claims with a BPC between w/c 2310 and w/c 2361 is either non-contentious or is adjudicated and allowed, the officer can establish a new claim without a disqualification using the hours from all the ROEs in the QP. If the dismissal or suspension is not allowed, the officer notifies the client of the decision verbally and in writing. When preparing the ACS letter, the officer chooses the attribute informing the client that the minimum number of hours is required to qualify for benefits, even when a new claim can be established.

In order for the dismissal to be adjudicated at Level 1, the client’s statement on the application must show that the client was dismissed for being unsuitable or due to a shortage of work. In addition, the employer’s statement or comments on the ROE must indicate that the client was dismissed for being unsuitable ( Not suitable , Did not pass training , or Terminated within the probationary period ) and there must not be any other contentious issues related to the dismissal that would prevent the Level 1 officer from allowing the reason for separation (RFS). If the client worked for the employer for 12 weeks or less and the employer or the comments on the ROE confirm that the RFS is unsuitability ( Not suitable , Did not pass training or Terminated within the probationary period ), the officer does not fact-find with the client, even if the client did not provide details regarding the employment on the EI application. The officer can allow the dismissal as long as there are no other contentious issues related to the dismissal. If the employer or ROE comments do not confirm unsuitability, or if the client worked for the employer for more than 12 weeks, the officer fact-finds with the client. For more information, the officer refers to the National Policy on Levels of Decision . National Policy on Levels of Decision The officer reviews the ROE to determine if there are comments showing that the client was dismissed for unsuitability or if the client’s employment was terminated in the probationary period. On a Web ROE, the employer can select the Terminated within probationary period field. If there is no indication on the ROE or if there is no ROE on file, the officer fact-finds with the employer. Clients can submit ROEs using the document upload feature in AW and MSCA. The system accepts only ROEs beginning with A, E, K, L, and Z. The serial number is also mandatory. The system does not check whether the serial number already exists in RCM. The officer can view uploaded ROEs on the Uploaded Documents tab in NWS. When clients upload ROEs in MSCA or in AW, an Action Item (AI) ROE Input WI is created in NWS. The officer completing the AI ROE Input WI views the ROE in NWS and inputs the ROE directly in RCM. If the ROE requires corrections or notes, the officer performs the action in RCM. This process does not involve RMDS. Note When clients upload their own paper ROE in AW or MSCA but the ROE was issued with the wrong SIN, officers fact-find with employers to confirm that they issued the ROE with the wrong SIN. Officers advise employers that a new or amended ROE is not required and they add an SROC in NWS confirming that the uploaded paper ROE with the wrong SIN belongs to the client. When clients upload another client’s ROE in AW or MSCA, it cannot be moved under the correct SIN. Officers contact the team leader to remove the document from view. For more information, officers refer to Document upload: Updating documents — Instructions . Document upload: Updating documents — Instructions

If clients want to extend their stay in Canada, they must apply to do so before the expiry date of their current permit. Clients can apply to do one of the following: extend their visitor, student or work status; change their permit type (e.g. from a study permit to a work permit); change their permit conditions (e.g. if they are studying and want to change schools, or if they are working and want to change jobs). Maintained status When foreign workers apply to renew their visitor visa, study permit or work permit on or before the expiration date and the permit expires before IRCC renders a decision, they can continue working under the same conditions while awaiting IRCC’s decision, as long as they remain in Canada. This is referred to as maintained status. In order to prove availability, they must provide proof of maintained status by submitting a copy of the expired work permit and one of the following: a copy of a courier receipt addressed to IRCC a copy of the client’s application to IRCC a copy of the fee receipt related to the application a copy of the letter sent by IRCC or a screenshot of the letter from the client’s IRCC account confirming the submission of the online application. Note If the client applied to renew a study or work permit on or before the expiration date, the client continues to have maintained status until IRCC renders a decision, even after IRCC processing times have passed. If IRCC denies the client’s application, the client no longer has maintained status from the date of the denial. Even if the client submits a new application for a work permit after IRCC denied the first application, maintained status cannot be granted if the work permit has already expired. In rare cases, IRCC may reject a client’s application to renew a work permit or study permit because it is incomplete. In this situation, the application is considered as never submitted and it cannot be considered to determine the maintained status. If the client had already been granted maintained status and benefits were paid, the Level 2 officer refers to Digest 17.3.3 to determine if it is necessary to impose a current or retroactive disentitlement. Digest 17.3.3 When clients receive IRCC’s response, they must update their SIN record so that the expiry date corresponds at all times with the one on the document received from IRCC that gives the authorization to work in Canada. Since the authorization to work in Canada has been received, clients can receive benefits even if the SIN record has not been updated. For more information about applications for extensions to work permits, maintained status and when maintained status ceases, the officer refers to the IRCC website . For information about the expiry date on the IRCC letter, the officer refers to Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: After you extend - Canada.ca . Eligible post-graduation work permit holders received an email in August 2022 from IRCC granting them interim work authorization until May 31, 2023. These clients are considered to have maintained status for EI purposes: If the permit expired between September 20, 2021 and October 1, 2022, proof that the client submitted an application to renew the work permit before December 31, 2022 is required. If the permit expired between October 2, 2022 and December 31, 2022 and the client had a valid passport and address on file with IRCC, no application is required and a new WP was automatically issued to the client. If the permit expired between October 2, 2022 and December 31, 2022 and the client did not have a valid passport or valid address on file with IRCC, proof that the client filed an application to renew the work permit is required. Eligible post-graduation work permit holders received an email in April 2023 from IRCC granting them interim work authorization until May 31, 2024. If it is determined that the client had good cause for failing to take advantage of a job opportunity, inform employers of their right to request a reconsideration of the decision if the reason is related to the employment. If the reason is strictly personal, no right to reconsideration is given to the employer.

If it is determined that the client had good cause for refusing an offer of employment, inform employers of their right to request a reconsideration of the decision if the reason is related to the employment. If the reason is strictly personal, no right to reconsideration is given to the employer.

The employment is suitable if no stoppage of work occurred at the site or when the employment offered is not normally performed by the workers involved in the labour dispute, even if a work stoppage and labour dispute exist. If it is determined that the job opportunity was not suitable, no disqualification is imposed.

Clients are not expected to seek or accept employment that is not suitable. To determine if the employment is suitable, consider the following criteria: Personal circumstances : Do the client’s health and physical capabilities allow them to commute to the place of work and to perform the work? Hours of work : Are the hours of work compatible with the client’s family obligations or religious beliefs? Working conditions : Is the nature of the work not contrary to the client’s moral convictions or religious beliefs? Furthermore, at the start of the BP, employment is not suitable if: It is in the client’s usual occupation but at a lower rate of pay or with less favorable conditions than the client’s previous employment or those offered by “good employers” for that type of work in the local labour market. It is not in the client’s usual occupation and is at a lower rate of pay or with less favorable conditions than the client might reasonably expect to obtain in the client’s usual occupation. When determining if the employment is suitable, the agent must consider all the facts, including: the type of work, conditions of employment, rate of pay, availability of that type of employment in the labour market, and commuting distance. After a reasonable period, employment that was deemed not suitable at the start of the BP may be considered suitable as long as the working conditions and rate of pay are comparable to those offered by good employers within the local labour market.

BCS allows certain types of transactions to be processed on blocked dormant claims. There are 2 options available: Estimate and Claim update . Updating a blocked claim When transactions must be input on a blocked claim, the Blocked tab in FTS must be reviewed to determine the BCS status. If the status of the claim is 1 - Updateable , an update is requested using BCS and the transactions can be processed. Note Different transactions may need to be input over multiple days to obtain the correct OP messages. When inputting multiple transactions, the following order must be respected: Callout An update in BCS can only be done on one BPC at a time. When transactions are input but not processed, Yes appears in the Block Action Pending column and access is denied for input on all other BPCs until requested transactions are processed. Access to a BPC with a pending action is limited to the agent who initiated that action. When updating a claim using BCS for misrepresentation cases, the agent must move the WI to Pending for the next day to allow BCS to calculate and establish the OP. Penalty inputs in PSCD and violation inputs in the Violation (ML01) transaction are done once the OP amount is known. Once the transactions have been processed, BCS displays information that can be used to determine the penalty amount. The Results tab displays the net OP amount. In addition, the Penalty link provides details about the OP amount that was established for weeks within the 36-month period, if part of the reconsideration period is beyond the limitation for imposing a monetary penalty. The Penalty determination window displays the net OP calculated for the 156-week period from the date the OP was established and from the current date. The information based on the current date can be used if there is a delay in reviewing the data and establishing the penalty. If an update is requested by the agent but cannot be completed by BCS, on the next processing day, the “Blocked claim not updated or not calculated” message is displayed along with the exception, error or warning on the MR05 screen. Agents review the exception, error or warning on the Results tab in BCS for further action. If the update cannot be completed using BCS, the system presents an estimate result. The decision can be sent to IPOC using the Forward via MM06 link which creates the prefilled Renewal/Revised ( M106) and MM06 transactions. Estimate function The Estimate function in BCS allows agents to view and evaluate the end results without processing the transactions. Estimates are possible for blocked claims with a 1 - Updateable status as well as unblocked dormant claims, provided the CS is 05 (inactive) or 06 (terminated) . BCS Estimate transactions are processed overnight and the results are available on the Results tab the next day. Agents that have requested an estimate can view the end result and forward the request for IPOC intervention using the prefilled MM06 available under the Results tab.

When clients report earnings on their claimant’s report, the earnings are coded along with an FWW code, if applicable. An FWW is coded if the client declared working 35 hours or more (28 hours or more in a week containing one of these 4 federal statutory holidays: New Year’s Day, Canada Day, Labour Day, Christmas Day). An investigation could reveal that FWWs have been coded when the client did not work or worked less than an FWW. When an FWW must be removed, document the decision on a record of decision (ROD).

This ensures that NIIS has a complete record of the investigation. It is important to note that the PSCD inputs, not the amounts entered on the Decision tab, update the penalty values on the Case Summary (IC08) screen in NIIS. If the penalty values are not automatically updated, they can be manually updated by a NIIS regional coordinator so that Integrity staff receive proper credit for their work. This implementation task applies to archived claims and blocked claims that are not updateable in BCS. It includes the following: creating an MM06 for IPOC to input of the reconsideration decision(s) and penalty inputting the reconsidered decision(s) in RCM (if applicable) sending the decision letter in ACS clearing the case in NIIS completing the WI in NWS Determining if there is collusion with a third party A third party making a misrepresentation with the client’s knowledge and consent is considered collusion. In this situation, the client must repay the net overpayment (OP) and any applicable sanction can be imposed on both the client and the third party. Updating the special condition in RCM If the reconsideration decision is related to the reason for separation (RFS) and the ROE is on file, the Special condition field must be updated in RCM to show the decision. The RCM input can be done at any time. Sending the file for recalculation Certain situations of misrepresentation (e.g. the submission of a false ROE or an ROE containing false information) require the claim to be recalculated. A recalculation is also required when the misrepresentation involves an undisclosed contentious RFS in the qualifying period (QP) and impacts the calculation of the claim. If a recalculation is required, an Action Item (AI) WI is created for Level 1. Once the recalculation transaction inputs have been determined by Level 1 and indicated in the client Note , a Level 2 officer creates the MM06 for IPOC to input the reconsideration decisions (including the recalculation) and the penalty. Communicating the decision On a blocked or archived claim, where the input is completed using an MM06, the officer is responsible for creating and saving the ACS letter(s) to notify the client of the reconsideration decisions and the penalty. The MM06 must clearly indicate whether IPOC should: send the saved ACS letter, add missing fields to the ACS letter, or amend and send the ACS letter. IPOC only sends the saved letter if advised to do so in the MM06. IPOC does not create the ACS letter. Completing the case in NIIS Level 2 officers have access to NIIS to view selected information and to complete cases they have adjudicated. Although the Level 2 decisions are documented in NWS, the Decision tab on the Report of Investigation ( IC50 or IC70 ) screen must be completed to close the case. This ensures that NIIS has a complete record of the investigation.

This implementation task applies to archived claims and blocked claims that are not updateable in BCS. It includes the following: creating an MM06 for IPOC to input the reconsideration decision(s) and the violation inputting the reconsidered decision(s) in RCM (if applicable) sending the decision letter in ACS clearing the case in NIIS completing the WI in NWS Determining if there is collusion with a third party A third party making a misrepresentation with the client’s knowledge and consent is considered collusion. In this situation, the client must repay the net overpayment (OP) and any applicable sanction can be imposed on both the client and the third party. Updating the special condition in RCM If the reconsideration decision is related to the reason for separation (RFS) and the ROE is on file, the Special condition field must be updated in RCM to show the decision. The RCM input can be done at any time. Sending the file for recalculation Certain situations of misrepresentation (e.g. the submission of a false ROE or an ROE containing false information) require the claim to be recalculated. A recalculation is also required when the misrepresentation involves an undisclosed contentious RFS in the qualifying period (QP) and impacts the calculation of the claim. If a recalculation is required, an Action Item (AI) WI is created for Level 1. Once the recalculation transaction inputs have been determined by Level 1 and indicated in the client Note , a Level 2 officer creates the MM06 for IPOC to input the reconsideration decisions (including the recalculation) and the violation. Communicating the decision On a blocked or archived claim, the officer is responsible for creating and saving the ACS letter(s) to notify the client of the reconsideration decisions and warning. The MM06 must clearly indicate whether IPOC should: send the saved ACS letter(s), add missing fields to the ACS letter(s), or amend and send the ACS letter(s). IPOC only sends the saved letter(s) if advised to do so in the MM06. IPOC does not create the ACS letter(s). When transactions must be input on a blocked claim, the officer reviews the Blocked Claims System tab in FTS to determine the BCS status. If the CS is 1 - Updateable , the officer requests an update using BCS and the transactions can be processed. Note In BCS, only one BPC can be updated at a time. When transactions are input but not processed, Yes appears in the Block Action Pending column and access is denied for input on all other BPCs until the requested transactions are processed. Access to a BPC with a pending action is limited to the officer who initiated that action. If the officer requests an update that cannot be completed by BCS, on the next processing day, the message Blocked claim not updated or not calculated is displayed along with the exception, error or warning on the Rejected Transactions Retrieval (MR05) screen. The officer reviews the exception, error or warning on the Results tab in BCS for further action. If the update cannot be completed using BCS, the system presents an estimate result. If the officer receives error code B112 , the officer creates an MM06 using a Renewal/Revised (M106) transaction. For other errors, the officer reviews WECS and re-inputs the transactions in BCS, or if necessary, sends the decision to IPOC using the Forward via MM06 link, which creates the prefilled M106 and MM06 transactions. If the client received the $2 000 advance payment, the officer reviews the Emergency Response Benefits screen in FTS to determine which code is displayed. Some of the lump sum payment modification codes are: A - Removed - SIN change B - Added - SIN change C - Cancelled D - Established as overpayment E - Received twice F - Received three or more times G - Removed - Victim of a third party fraud I - Removed - Exceptional or multiple condition(s) / Non-fraud third party overpayment N - $1500 established as overpayment P - $1000 established as overpayment Q - $500 established as overpayment The OP created by the disentitlement does not include the $2 000 advance payment,if it was paid. If the $2 000 advance payment was issued and the lump sum payment modification code is C , D , G , or I , the officer imposes the disentitlement in BCS. If the lump sum payment modification code is blank, B , N , P or Q , the officer may have to send the information to IPOC on an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction. The processing officer inputs transactions in BCS but may receive error code B112 . This code prevents amendments to the file before the 65 - Lump Sum Payment ($2000) - Canadian Emergency Response code (D65) logic is removed from the claim. If the officer receives error code B112 after attempting to input transactions in BCS, the officer sends an MM06 to request IPOC intervention. The IPOC officer updates the lump sum payment modification code to D and inputs the remaining transactions. For more information on the lump sum payment modification code, the officer refers to COVID-19: Emergency Response Advance Payment Modification — Knowledge . COVID-19: Emergency Response Advance Payment Modification — Knowledge If a W - Earnings week 1 allocation is on file, the officer inputs an A - Amended earnings allocation in BCS with 0000 in the Earnings field.

An archived payment is not accessible when the payment reference number is input. The officer receives an AYE05007 No payment records found message. To access archived payments, from the Main Menu drop-down menu, the IPOC officer selects Payment Enquiry and, from the Screen drop-down menu, selects Payment Information Enquiry . Then, the IPOC officer inputs the client’s SIN, checks the Archived Payments Only box and selects Go . Occasionally, a payment is archived and must be restored to initiate the trace request. To restore an archived payment, the IPOC officer selects the appropriate payment reference number, which brings the officer to the Request to Restore Payments screen, and the officer selects Confirm . The IPOC officer can also access this screen by selecting Restore Archived Data from the Main Menu drop-down menu and Request to Restore Payments from the Screen drop-down menu. SPS processes requests to restore payments every half hour. To determine if the payment information has been restored, from the Main Menu drop-down menu, the IPOC officer selects Payment Enquiry , and from the Screen drop-down menu, selects Payment Information Detail Enquiry and inputs the payment reference number in question. If the payment information appears, the payment has been restored.

BCS allows certain types of transactions to be processed on blocked, dormant claims. There are 2 options available: Estimate and Claim update . Accessibility depends on the CS in BCS. When modifications are only required to earnings or when modifying an FWW code for a week of regular benefits, if the claim is a blocked claim and the CS in BCS is 1 - Updateable , the agent can request an update using BCS and the transactions can be processed. When the CS in BCS is 2 - Not blocked , the agent reactivates the claim and inputs the decision as on an active claim. For any other BCS CS, the agent sends an MM06 to IPOC to process the transactionsMM06.

The minimum living allowance is the threshold below which no AOB recoupments can be taken from a client’s EI benefits. The regional social services agency determines the start week and the amount of the minimum living allowance and documents this information on the INS3113 form. The minimum living allowance affects only the recoupment of AOB amounts and does not prevent other deductions from reducing a client’s net EI benefits. A minimum living allowance is not required when completing the INS3113 form, but if it is provided, both the Amount $ and Effective Date fields must be completed by the social services agency. If only one of the 2 fields has been completed, the AOB request must be returned to the sender, indicating the reason for the return. If there is no claim on file or if the Assignment of Benefits link is grey, the officer completes the Minimum living allowance - Effective week field on the T173.

Clients who have applied for EI benefits can also request financial assistance from social services. Clients must sign a form to authorize deductions from their EI benefits to reimburse social services for the social assistance received in weeks for which EI benefits are also paid. When an AOB is input in CPS, all or a portion of a client’s weekly EI benefit payment is recouped and reimbursed to a social services agency. Assignment of Benefits (INS3113) form To request an AOB, the social services worker completes the Assignment of benefits: INS3113 Request from social services agency — Form with the client and mails or couriers it directly to IPOC. Assignment of benefits: INS3113 Request from social services agency — Form Note When an INS3113 form cannot be validated, is illegible or is missing information, the IPOC officer returns it to the social services agency for correction. The INS3113 form provides the following: client’s SIN, first name and last name; 4-digit social services office number; name, telephone number and address of the social services agency; social services agency worker’s signature; client’s authorization of AOB deductions and consent to the disclosure and use of personal information; amounts paid by social services; weekly AOB amounts; start week and end week of the AOB request; last week amount, if necessary; minimum living allowance amount and its effective week, if necessary. To be consistent with the EI payment schedule, the amounts to be reimbursed are requested in a calendar weekly format (Sunday to Saturday).

The social services office number is provided on the INS3113 form and entered on the Assignment of Benefits — Input (T173) transaction in FTS. It is used by accounting operations in the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) and by external partners to correctly direct monies recouped for AOB. Both the provincial social service agency and the CFOB use this 4-digit number to manage the flow of money between the various departments and offices. As FTS accepts any combination of numbers or letters input into this field without rejection, the IPOC officer must confirm that the proper code is input during data entry of an AOB. If the number provided by the social services agency is unclear or unable to be verified on a regional office code list, the AOB request must be returned to the sender without being processed.

If one of the following conditions applies, the claimant’s report is considered unacceptable. Early paper claimant’s reports A claimant’s report received before the last Friday of the period covered is considered early, with the following exceptions: The client found work during the current week and the earnings declared are above the no benefits payable amount. No benefits are payable for that week. The client is deceased. When a claimant’s report is received early and the exceptions do not apply, the claimant’s report indicating the correct mailing date is returned to the client. Incomplete or incorrect claimant’s reports A claimant’s report is considered incomplete or incorrect in the following situations: The client has not answered one question or more. The client has answered the questions, but failed to provide further details or the answers are incomplete (accepted if there are no benefits payable). The client has reported a return to work (RTW) on a day other than the Monday of week 1 or 2 and has not indicated earnings from that employment. The dates worked and reported earnings are shown in the wrong week. The client reports information in the For office use section and the same information is not shown in the appropriate section on the claimant’s report. The client indicated the total hours worked or dates but no earnings are declared (accepted if there are no benefits payable). Late claimant’s reports The claimant’s report week of issue, week 1 date and date of receipt are all used to determine whether the claimant’s report is received late. The week of issue is shown in the N box on the paper claimant’s report. Calculating the time period for late claimant’s reports The time period is calculated in one of two ways, depending on the date of issue and week 1 of the claimant’s report: When the first week of the claimant’s report is equal to or less than the week of issue, it is considered received late if the difference between the week received and the week of issue is 6 weeks or greater. When the first week of the claimant’s report is greater than the week of issue, the claimant’s report is considered late if the difference between the week received and the first week of the claimant’s report is equal to or greater than 6 weeks. If the claimant’s report is not received in 5 weeks or less, it is considered late, with the following exceptions: The client found work and no benefits are payable for the weeks of the claimant’s report. The claimant’s report was previously returned to the client and the date is within 6 weeks of the current w/c. There are multiple claimants’ reports and not all were received late. The ANT (apprentice with advance payments) or APP (apprentice) code appears in the APP box in the For Office Use Only section of the paper claimant’s report. The claimant’s report was issued manually (i.e. hand-written by the Service Canada Centre [SCC]). Missing signature on the paper claimant’s report Unsigned claimant’s reports are accepted and processed if: The client is exempt from reporting (NO-CR-CODE). The claimant’s report was verified with the client. Other unacceptable claimant’s reports If one of the following conditions applies, the IPOC officer does not input the claimant’s report. In that case, the IPOC officer creates an AI WI for Level 1. The other unacceptable claimant’s reports include: the claimant’s report is out of sequence; the client reports training, but no project information is on file; the client reports being absent from home or out of Canada between Monday and Friday; there is a return to work (RTW) date on file and client did not report earnings on or after that date.

If an Assessment Issue (ASMT) Insurability WI is automatically created because of the information on the client’s application, the claim cannot be automated unless the officer updates the Status field of the ROE. When the officer requests an insurability ruling and the related ROE is on file, the officer updates the Status field of the ROE in RCM to indicate that an insurability ruling is pending. During automation, ACP first determines if an ROE with the status Insurability Ruling Pending is on file. If yes, ACP remains in the wait process until the status of that ROE is updated to either VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order . Once the officer updates the ROE, ACP resumes the automation process. When the Status field of the ROE shows Insurability Ruling Pending , SSO excludes the ROE from the manual calculation. If there are no ROEs with status Insurability Ruling Pending , ACP determines if the client answered Yes to the business relationship question on the EI application. If the client answered Yes and there are no ROEs on file with the status VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order , ACP remains in the wait process until the status of an ROE in the qualifying period (QP) is updated to either VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order . If an insurability ruling is not required and there is no doubt that the employment is insurable, the officer updates the Status field of the ROE to display Insurability in Order . If an insurability ruling is not required and there is no doubt that the employment is insurable, but the ROE is not on file, the officer moves the ASMT Insurability WI to Pending until either the ROE is received or the ACP wait process ends, whichever comes first. If the ROE is received first, the officer updates the Status field of the ROE to Insurability in Order . If the wait process ends first, no further action is required.

If yes, ACP remains in the wait process until the status of that ROE is updated to either VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order . Once the officer updates the ROE, ACP resumes the automation process. When the Status field of the ROE shows Insurability Ruling Pending , SSO excludes the ROE from the manual calculation. If there are no ROEs with status Insurability Ruling Pending , ACP determines if the client answered Yes to the business relationship question on the EI application. If the client answered Yes and there are no ROEs on file with the status VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order , ACP remains in the wait process until the status of an ROE in the qualifying period (QP) is updated to either VOID - Not Insurable or Insurability in Order . If an insurability ruling is not required and there is no doubt that the employment is insurable, the officer updates the Status field of the ROE to display Insurability in Order . If an insurability ruling is not required and there is no doubt that the employment is insurable, but the ROE is not on file, the officer moves the ASMT Insurability WI to Pending until either the ROE is received or the ACP wait process ends, whichever comes first. If the ROE is received first, the officer updates the Status field of the ROE to Insurability in Order . If the wait process ends first, no further action is required.

Foreign workers are responsible for proving they were authorized to work in Canada for all periods of employment in their QP. Any of the following documents are acceptable proof: a copy of the work permit (IMM1442 or IMM1102) a copy of a Temporary Resident Visa for individuals who are authorized to work without a work permit. To prove maintained status, the client must provide one of the following documents: a copy of a courier receipt addressed to IRCC a copy of the client’s application to IRCC a copy of the fee receipt related to the application a copy of the letter sent by IRCC confirming the submission of the online application To prove maintained status for insurability purposes in the QP, the client may also provide the following document: a copy of the current work permit containing a reference indicating the temporary resident status was maintained per Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations 183(5) or 183(6). It is the client’s responsibility to obtain copies of the employment authorization from IRCC. The officer does not contact IRCC on behalf of a client. Note

If they want to continue working in Canada, clients whose work permit is expiring must apply to have it renewed. Clients who apply to have their work permit renewed before its expiration date have maintained status while they are waiting for the renewal to be processed, as long as they remain in Canada. A client with maintained status can continue to legally work in Canada under the same conditions as those of the prior work permit. The client’s maintained status lasts until IRCC makes a decision on the work permit renewal. If the client applied to renew a study or work permit on or before the expiration date, the client continues to have maintained status until IRCC renders a decision, even after IRCC processing times have passed. If IRCC denies the client’s application, the client no longer has maintained status from the date of the denial. Even if the client submits a new application for a work permit after IRCC denied the first application, maintained status cannot be granted if the work permit has already expired. In rare cases, IRCC may reject a client’s application to renew a work permit or study permit because it is incomplete. In this situation, the application is considered as never submitted and it cannot be considered to determine maintained status. If the client had already been granted maintained status and benefits were paid, the Level 2 officer refers to the Digest 17.3.3 to determine if it is necessary to impose a current or retroactive disentitlement. Digest 17.3.3 For more information on maintained status, the officer can refer to Insurability Policy — Employment of Foreign Nationals in Canada - Immigrant Work Permit . Insurability Policy — Employment of Foreign Nationals in Canada - Immigrant Work Permit Work permit containing a reference to Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations 183(5) or 183(6) If a foreign worker has had more than one work permit in the QP, there may be a gap between the end date of the previous work permit and the start date of the current work permit. A reference on the current work permit indicating that the temporary resident status was maintained during the gap per Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations 183(5) or 183(6) renders any work during that period insurable. The officer uses this information to confirm maintained status for insurability purposes in the QP. Therefore, it is the client’s responsibility to provide proof of the authorization to work in Canada during the period or periods during which the client was employed. Temporary process for post-graduate work permit holders Foreign workers whose post-graduation work permit expires between September 20, 2021 and December 31, 2023 can work in Canada for an additional 18 months or until the expiry of their passport, whichever comes first. Eligible post-graduation work permit holders receive an email from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) granting them interim work authorization until December 31, 2023. These clients are considered to have maintained status for EI purposes. The authorization can be extended until May 31, 2024, if the client submits the authorization email and any required proof based when the client’s permit expired: If it expired between September 20, 2021, and October 1, 2022 proof that the client submitted an application to renew the work permit before December 31, 2022 is required. If it expired between October 2, 2022, and December 31, 2022 and the client had a valid passport and address on file with IRCC no application is required and a new WP was automatically issued to the client. If it expired between October 2, 2022, and December 31, 2022 and the client did not have a valid passport or valid address on file with IRCC proof of an application to renew the work permit is required. If it expired after December 31, 2022, proof that the client registered through the simplified process (before May 21, 2023) or proof that the client submitted an application to renew the work permit is required. Note In order for the client to be granted maintained status until May 31, 2024, the client needs to provide the following documents: a copy of the work permit; a copy of the IRCC’s interim work authorization email; and one of the following based on the case: proof of application for a new work permit or a renewal proof of registration through the simplified process a statement from the client that they were not required to submit an application (valid passport and address) A new work permit If a client’s work permit expires before the receipt of the email from IRCC, the client must provide proof of an authorization to remain in Canada by means of a visitor’s permit, a study permit or another work permit. Note

If the agent rescinds a penalty and changes the case from misrepresentation to non-misrepresentation, the agent must ensure that any subsequent penalties are amended accordingly. For example, when a penalty is rescinded, a subsequent penalty, which was calculated at 100% for the second infraction, must now be recalculated as a first level misrepresentation at 50%. When a penalty is rescinded, any penalty amount that was recouped from benefits paid or repaid in cash is refunded to the client as long as there is no other outstanding OP to be repaid. When the case is changed from misrepresentation to non-misrepresentation, any interest that was applied is also reversed and refunded.

If the agent rescinds a penalty and changes the case from misrepresentation to voluntary disclosure, the agent must ensure that any subsequent penalties are amended accordingly. For example, when a penalty is rescinded, a subsequent penalty, which was calculated at 100% for the second infraction, must now be recalculated as a first level misrepresentation at 50%. When a penalty is rescinded, any penalty amount that was recouped is refunded to the client as long as there is no other outstanding OP to be repaid.

When a case is a first infraction and is changed from misrepresentation to non-misrepresentation, any violations subsequently imposed may be affected. If there is a violation following the rescinded violation, that subsequent violation is now considered to be the first infraction. When the agent rescinds a violation on the Violation (ML01) screen in FTS, a report is generated for IPOC review. Any violation imposed after the rescinded violation is adjusted automatically to reflect the new decision. An IPOC officer then determines if subsequent claims that were BPNE because of the increased entrance requirement must now be recalculated. If recalculation is required, an IPOC officer creates an Action Item (AI) WI for a Level 1 agent to perform the recalculation. For example, a minor violation is on file for a first infraction and there is a subsequent violation for a second infraction. The client provides new facts on the first infraction and as a result, the case is changed from misrepresentation to non-misrepresentation. The violation for the first infraction is rescinded which results in the second infraction now becoming the first infraction. The agent reviews any subsequent BPNE claims to determine if the removal of the violation results in the claim no longer being BPNE.

When a case is a first infraction and is changed from misrepresentation to voluntary disclosure, any violations subsequently imposed may be affected. If there is a violation following the rescinded violation, that subsequent violation is now considered to be the first infraction. When the agent rescinds a violation on the Violation (ML01) screen in FTS, a report is generated for IPOC review. Any violation imposed after the rescinded violation is adjusted automatically to reflect the new level of misrepresentation. An IPOC officer then determines if subsequent claims that were BPNE because of the increased entrance requirement must now be recalculated. If recalculation is required, an IPOC officer creates an Action Item WI for a Level 1 agent to perform the recalculation. For example, a minor violation is on file for a first offense and there is a subsequent violation for a second infraction. The client provides new facts on the first infraction and as a result, the case is changed from misrepresentation to voluntary disclosure. The violation for the first infraction is rescinded which results in the second infraction now becoming the first infraction. The agent reviews any subsequent BPNE claims to determine if the removal of the violation results in the claim no longer being BPNE.

A Budget 2021 measure applies to separation monies that are reviewed between September 26, 2021 (w/c 2310) and September 24, 2022 (w/c 2361) and are paid due to a temporary layoff or a permanent separation from employment. When separation monies are reviewed during that period, they are not considered earnings and are not allocated, regardless of the BPC. Separation monies that are not allocated cannot extend a benefit period (BP). This measure applies to all benefit types (BTs) for initial, renewal and continuing claims. However, if the information reviewed affects a previous allocation (i.e. changes the allocation amount), the rules that applied to that claim when the monies were initially input still apply.

A Budget 2021 measure applies to separation monies that are reviewed between September 26, 2021 (w/c 2310) and September 24, 2022 (w/c 2361) and are paid due to a temporary layoff or a permanent separation from employment. When separation monies are reviewed during that period, they are not considered earnings and are not allocated, regardless of the BPC. Separation monies that are not allocated cannot extend a benefit period (BP). This measure applies to all benefit types (BTs) for initial, renewal and continuing claims. However, if the information reviewed affects a previous allocation (i.e. changes the allocation amount), the rules that applied to that claim when the monies were originally allocated still apply. Vacation pay that is paid on separation is not allocated. All other vacation pay (e.g. vacation pay that is included with each pay or that is paid on a specific date each year) is allocated according to regular procedures.

If funds for a week of payable EI benefits have been recouped and reimbursed to the social services office, the original AOB amount for that week cannot be modified. However, a modification of the AOB weekly amount is possible if no EI benefits were paid or payable on the original claimant’s report. Since no recoupments are made nor a dual payment amount calculated, CPS accepts the modification as though the claimant’s reports have never been processed. For example, a client who was not originally entitled to payment due to an EI decision (e.g. disentitlement, disqualification) or a condition declared on the claimant’s report may now qualify for payment due to a revised decision or an amended claimant’s report. In these cases, the dual payment amount is recalculated because the client was not originally paid. When an officer amends or reconsiders an EI decision such that a client is no longer entitled to EI benefits for a week for which an AOB has been recouped, an overpayment (OP) including the amount paid to social services is created.

To establish their entitlement, it is necessary to determine if clients would have been available for work if they had been capable of working. Clients must prove that they would be otherwise available for work for each day in the period of incapacity. They cannot provide proof of capability weeks or months in advance. The information provided must be reviewed to determine if clients have proven their availability. The decision is made on the credibility of the information given. If the facts prove that clients would otherwise be available for work, the officer accepts the information.

If a pregnant client has stopped working because of incapacity, she is considered otherwise available for work until the earlier of the following dates: the week before the expected date of birth (DOB); the week before the actual DOB (if it is on file). However, if any part of the client’s incapacity falls in the period of prearranged maternity leave, she is not considered otherwise available for work during the entire period of the prearranged maternity leave , and is therefore not entitled to sickness benefits during that period. She is still entitled to maternity benefits during the period of prearranged maternity leave. When a client is considered otherwise available during the maternity window, an external maternity start week is required to prevent the payment of maternity benefits while the client is entitled to benefits other than maternity. Example If the client specifically requests sickness benefits for the week of birth, the Level 1 officer can allow the payment of sickness benefits in that week if the actual DOB was the Saturday of that week. If the DOB is any other day of the week, or if the client is requesting sickness benefits beyond the week of birth, the Level 1 officer refers the question to Level 2. Minor attached client Sickness benefits can be paid for the 14-day period following the DOB when a minor-attached client is receiving regular benefits in the maternity window. A medical certificate is not required to allow this 14-day period, but the client is still required to prove that she is otherwise available for work on each day she requests sickness benefits. Only Level 2 officers can make these decisions. Clients who request sickness benefits during the PW, CCW or FCW are not required to prove they would be otherwise available for work, as long as they remain entitled to those benefits. When the sickness period extends beyond the window established for those benefits, or they have exhausted entitlement to those benefits, clients must prove that they are otherwise available to work during that period. They must also provide a medical certificate indicating the start date of their incapacity. Clients who are not entitled to parental benefits, CCB, or family caregiver benefits must prove that they are available for work to receive regular benefits. If a client is disentitled from regular benefits due to availability and then requests sickness benefits, the client is considered not otherwise available for work and the officer imposes a disentitlement during the period of sickness unless the client proves that the situation has changed since the original decision. A client who is outside of Canada can receive parental benefits as long as the client meets the entitlement conditions to receive these benefits. A client receiving parental benefits is not required to prove availability for work, and will not be disentitled for the sole reason of being out of Canada. However, the client must continue to care for the child for whom the benefits are payable.

A client who is outside of Canada can receive family caregiver benefits as long as the client meets the entitlement conditions for these benefits. A client receiving family caregiver benefits is not required to prove availability for work, and is not disentitled for the sole reason of being out of Canada. However, the client must continue to provide care or support to the patient for whom the benefits are payable.

An electronic questionnaire is presented through IRS or MSCA to clients when they report an absence from Canada. Automated adjudication may allow the absence from Canada or impose definite or indefinite disentitlements preventing payment during the period of the absence, excluding the departure and return dates, on established and skeleton claims. It may also terminate indefinite disentitlements when clients report that they have returned to Canada. An automated ROD is created in NWS and stored on the electronic application for all automated decisions. When the decision cannot be automated the system imposes a stop payment and creates the appropriate WI; an Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI on initial or renewal claims, and a Claim Review Revised Availability WI on continuing claims.

Terminating an existing indefinite disentitlement for out of Canada situations is based on clients’ declaration of returning to the country and confirmation of availability for work. If clients are receiving sickness benefits, they must also confirm that, if not for the illness, they would be working or available for work. The 13 - Outside Canada disentitlement (D13) is not imposed for the date of departure or the date of return. When terminating a D13, the end date is the day before clients have returned to Canada. There may be other related issues that need to be addressed when a client returns to Canada, including: outstanding claimant reports (before the disentitlement — where payment could be blocked by a renewal input); late claimant reports (if there is a failure to report indicator on the claim); renewal of the claim (if there is a gap in claimant reports); availability/entitlement upon return to Canada (if there is any indication in NWS or Imaging that the client is not entitled to benefits upon return); entitlement for the period of absence from Canada if the purpose of the absence was to undergo medical treatment (proof that the medical treatment was administered).

Request from an unauthorized third party If a request for reconsideration is received from a third party without the appropriate requester’s signature and authorization of the interested party, it is considered to be an invalid request and the reconsideration under EIA 112 is not performed. EIA 112 No initial decision At times the Commission may receive a request to reconsider a decision before an initial decision has been made. In these cases, the reconsideration under EIA 112 cannot be performed because there is no initial decision to reconsider. This also applies to requests received when a reconsideration under EIA 112 has already been performed on the same issue (even if by another requester), but the request is related to a different time period (e.g. after the date of the reconsideration under EIA 112 decision). EIA 112 EIA 112 EIA 112 If the notice of the initial decision was not sent, but the record shows that the Commission made a decision on the issue being challenged, the request for reconsideration is accepted and processed. The notice of the initial decision is not sent at this point. The notice of decision on the reconsideration sets the record straight. Issues outside the Commission’s authority At times a request may be received to review a decision that is related to an EI claim, but that is outside the Commission’s authority to review. These include the following: insurability of employment, hours and earnings benefit repayment (claw back) responsibility of repayment and interest charged on an OP During the course of the reconsideration under EIA 112 , the officer may have to determine if an issue is outside the Commission’s authority, and whether the request for reconsideration can be held in abeyance while waiting for a decision on another matter. EIA 112 The officer always reconsiders a decision that resulted in an OP regardless of the reason the client gave for the request for reconsideration and whether the client is expressly disputing the obligation to repay the debt. Obligation to repay an overpayment (OP) When the client disputes the obligation to repay an OP, the officer: reconsiders the decision that led to the OP; reviews the calculation of the OP to make sure it is accurate; adjudicates a formally requested write-off of the OP. In addition, the officer must include a breakdown of the OP in the following situations and add the information to the reconsideration file: the client disputes the OP amount; the OP amount changed during the process after the initial decision; the OP calculation is complex. Decisions not subject to reconsideration under EIA 112 A request may be received to review a decision that is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . The following decisions are not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 : EIA 112 EIA 112 Work-sharing (WS) agreement: A decision about the approval or refusal of a WS agreement is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . EIA 112 EIA 25 referral: A decision about the referral of a client to a course, program or other employment activity under EIA 25 is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . These issues must be resolved with the referring authority. EIA 25 EIA 112 Pilot Project: Working While on Claim: A decision about a reversion under Pilot Project: Working While on Claim is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . This includes the denial of a request for reversion, the denial of a late request for reversion, and a request to undo a reversion. EIA 112 Write-off: A decision about writing off a penalty owed, amount payable or interest accrued on any penalty owed or amount payable is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . The client’s recourse regarding these issues is to seek judicial review with the Federal Court of Canada. EIA 112 Payment refusal requests: The decision to impose a D21 is discretionary. Denial of a payment refusal request is a decision that is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . The client’s recourse regarding this issue is to seek judicial review with the Federal Court of Canada. EIA 112 Voluntary disclosure: A decision to accept or refuse information under the voluntary disclosure policy is not subject to a reconsideration under EIA 112 . The client’s recourse regarding this issue is to seek judicial review with the Federal Court of Canada. EIA 112 The decision on the request for reconsideration reflects the Commission’s position and informs the client of the proper recourse. The client does not have the right to appeal in the above situations, and appeal rights are not mentioned in the letter of decision. Nevertheless, the client can still choose to file an appeal. It is the responsibility of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal (EI BOA) or Social Security Tribunal (SST) to decide whether the appeal will proceed or be dismissed. Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms The Commission does not address any issues regarding the application of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms. The reconsideration under EIA 112 proceeds only on the substantive issues. EIA 112

According to the legislation, a requester must request a review within 30 calendar days of the communication of the initial decision. The Commission considers delays between 31 and 120 days to be short delays and approves the delay without further fact-finding. This period may be extended if the requester provides a reasonable explanation. The request period starts on the earliest date the client, the employer or other person subject to the initial decision becomes aware of it: the date of the verbal communication, whether it is followed by a letter or not; the date the notice of decision is received; the date the NOD is received, if the notice of decision was not received and the request for reconsideration is linked to the OP or penalty amount.

During the reconsideration process under EIA 112 , the officer may come across one or more of the following 3 situations: EIA 112 an issue not previously identified or adjudicated; a new issue that requires adjudication before benefits can be paid, in cases where the initial decision is being changed; an error unrelated to the decision being reviewed. The officer can address an outstanding issue at the time of the reconsideration under EIA 112 only if it is essential in order to resolve the issue under review, or if the same facts and circumstances taken into consideration for the initial decision lead the reconsideration officer to another outcome, because the issues are inherently linked or there is an interconnected issue. EIA 112 In all other cases, the issue must be referred to Processing for review . When referring an issue to processing, the officer must exercise judgment and consider imposing a manual action in order to avoid paying benefits if there is a decision that remains to be adjudicated. referred to Processing for review Processing issues considered to be inherently linked The following are examples of issues considered to be inherently linked that must be addressed at the time of the reconsideration under EIA 112 . EIA 112 Example 1: BPNE and implied antedate A reconsideration under EIA 112 is being performed on a decision about BPNE. During fact-finding, the client implies that they want an antedate, and it may be possible to establish a claim if the antedate is granted. The officer must therefore address both issues because they are inherently linked. The officer completes all necessary fact-finding, makes a decision and informs the client of both decisions. If the decisions are negative, the officer provides appeal rights to the client on both issues. If the antedate is allowed, the officer completes the ROD as per adjudication procedures but only notifies the client that the BPNE decision has been rescinded in the decision letter. EIA 112 Example 2: Misconduct and voluntary leaving A reconsideration under EIA 112 is being performed on a decision about a dismissal, but during fact-finding, the officer finds the issue is really voluntary leaving. As both issues are subject to EIA 30(1) , the officer makes a decision on the voluntary leaving. According to EIA 112 , clients, employers or any other person subject to a decision of the Commission have the right to ask for a reconsideration under EIA 112 of a claim decision. In the reconsideration under EIA 112 , the “requester” is the person making the request for reconsideration. When a request for reconsideration is received, an officer, different from the one who made the initial decision, performs a reconsideration under EIA 112 of the initial decision to ensure it follows the appropriate legislation and policies. EIA 112 EIA 112 EIA 112 EIA 112 The request for reconsideration must be submitted in writing. However, use of the Reconsideration: INS5210 Request for reconsideration of an EI decision — Form is not mandatory. If this form is not used, the request must be submitted in a letter that clearly states that it is a request for reconsideration and that includes the following information: Reconsideration: INS5210 Request for reconsideration of an EI decision — Form name of the requester (and the third party, if necessary) requester’s SIN or business number, address and telephone number date on which the decision was communicated to the requester The letter submitted must also include the reasons why the requester is requesting a reconsideration under EIA 112 of the decision. EIA 112 If the INS5210 was not used, and the intent of the letter is unclear, the issue is referred to processing for action. INS5210 An unsigned request for reconsideration is not automatically invalid, as there is no legislated requirement for a signature. Identity can be confirmed by cross-checking information already on file. If there is any question on the intent or authenticity of the letter, the officer contacts the requester for confirmation. A request for reconsideration faxed or submitted in any other electronic format is accepted and processed as long as there is no question as to its authenticity. Once a request for reconsideration is received, it cannot be withdrawn unless it was submitted in error. A request for reconsideration is considered to have been submitted in error only if the requester indicates at the start of the conversation that the letter was never meant to be a request for reconsideration. If it was the requester’s intent to request a reconsideration, but they state at the start of the conversation with the officer that they no longer wish to pursue the request, the Commission is nevertheless legally required to process the request. Note There are times when the processing centre may take action on a file without realizing that a reconsideration under EIA 112 has been requested. If this occurs, the officer processing the request for reconsideration must refer to Assessing whether a reconsideration under EIA 112 is required when an initial decision has been modified to determine if the reconsideration under 112 will proceed. If the reconsideration proceeds, the officer refers back to the Performing a reconsideration under EIA 112 . The definition of “employer” is limited to a person or organization for whom the client works or has worked. An employer is considered an interested party in the following cases and must be added as a participant in ADMS regardless of the outcome of the reconsideration under EIA 112 : EIA 112 dismissal voluntary leaving when the reasons for leaving are work-related refusal to accept employment or failure to take advantage of a job opportunity if the reasons for doing so are work-related labour disputes Employers are only notified if the decision is favourable to the client. However, the reconsideration under EIA 112 can still proceed in cases where the employer was not notified of the original decision but has requested a reconsideration of that decision. EIA 112 A potential or prospective employer for whom the client has not worked is not notified of the decision or of any further recourse action. Although the information gathered in the fact-finding process and taken into account in the decision is included in the reconsideration file, the employer is not considered to be an interested party.

Once deducted from a client’s EI benefits, assignment of benefits (AOB) recoupments cannot be reversed. If an AOB was over-deducted or deducted in error, the monies are sent to the appropriate social services agency and the social services officer refunds the client. Requests to amend family order agreement (FOA) recoupments originate from the Department of Justice. If FOA was over-deducted, an officer from the centralized FOA unit creates an MM06 with instructions to remove or reduce the FOA recoupment amount. Before contacting clients to validate their identity, officers determine if the application is already under investigation for potential fraud. Officers can determine that there is an ongoing Integrity investigation for this application if: In Curam, a suspension or 71 - Integrity services case disentitlement (D71) is imposed; An Investigation/Caution flag is displayed in Curam; in NWS, an SROC created by Integrity is on file; in NWS, an Action Item (AI) is assigned to Integrity; in NWS, a Call Back (CB) is assigned to Integrity. If none of these are on the file, officers review the file to determine if fraud indicators are present.
